items.title: Material Management
items.context: Material Management

cards.title: What the Material Management module covers
cards.body:
Material Management covers materials, purchasing, stores, quality inspection and the master data they share.
It takes a need from a department request through sourcing, ordering, gate inward, receipt, inspection and storage to issue, transfer and stock correction.
Its stock and receipts also feed Plant Maintenance, which draws spares from the same stores.

cards.title: Who works in Material Management and what they own
cards.body:
Department requesters raise material and purchase requests, and purchase officers source and order against them.
Purchase managers authorise orders, agreements and comparative statements within their approval limits.
Storekeepers and security staff record gate movements, receipts, issues, returns and transfers, while quality controllers inspect incoming goods.
Planners maintain stock levels and automatic replenishment, and master data owners keep items, vendors and units consistent.

cards.title: Why master data comes first in Material Management
cards.body:
Every transaction depends on master data set up beforehand: units, the category, group and sub group hierarchy, items, makes, tax codes, warehouses, bins and vendors.
Sub groups carry approved vendors, makes, units, tax codes and storage behaviour, so items under them inherit consistent rules.
Vendors need a card, at least one location with tax registration and contact persons before they can be invited or ordered from.
Quality parameters and specifications must exist before receipts can be inspected against them.
Getting this foundation right means requests, orders and receipts validate cleanly instead of failing on missing references.

cards.title: Common document lifecycle and authorisation pattern
cards.body:
Most transaction documents move through Initial, Release and Authorized, with each step stamping the user and time.
An authorised document is locked; later commercial changes go through an amendment or revision document so the original stays on record.
Downstream documents only pick up authorised, open source lines, and balances are reduced as each source is consumed.
Deletion is refused once a later document refers to the record, which preserves an end-to-end audit trail from request to stock.

cards.title: How demand, purchasing, receipt and stock link end to end
cards.body:
Demand starts as a material request; what the store cannot issue becomes a purchase request checked against budget, or is raised automatically from planned stock levels.
Buyers invite vendors through a request for quotation, record and compare quotations, and book the winning offers into a purchase order or use an existing rate agreement.
At the gate the inward vehicle and documents are recorded, the receipt note confirms quantities, and quality inspection decides what is accepted into stock.
Accepted lots carry value, which moves with every issue, return, transfer and adjustment, while freight and expenses on the order feed the landed rate.
Each step consumes the open balance of the step before it, so ordered, received and issued quantities can always be traced back to the original need.

items.title: Material Master Data Setup
items.context: Material Management › Material Master Data Setup

cards.title: Purpose of the material master setup flow
cards.body:
Material master data is built top-down: units, then categories, groups and sub groups, then items with makes, tariff and tax codes, technical grades and attribute values.
Master data owners run this flow before any request, order or receipt is entered.
Every transaction then refers to one clean, consistent item definition.

cards.title: Setup sequence and what items inherit
cards.body:
Units of measure and their conversion factors come first, because items, purchases and stock all report in them.
Categories and other short lists are defined next, then material groups and sub groups.
Sub groups hold approved vendors, makes, units, tax codes and storage settings, so items created under them inherit those choices.
Makes, chapter headings, HSN or SAC codes and technical specification heads are then available when the item is created, and attribute standard values complete the description.

cards.title: How tax codes flow from master data into orders and bills
cards.body:
Goods and service tax starts in master data: sub groups and items carry an HSN or SAC code, and units carry the reporting unit used for tax returns.
Each HSN or SAC code holds the applicable rates, while taxes, duties and charges are grouped and given account rules.
When a purchase order is created, the item's code determines the rate, and the vendor's and company's states decide whether central and state tax or integrated tax applies.
The purchase bill picks up the same structure to post taxes to the correct accounts.
A wrong code at master level therefore flows into every order, receipt and bill for that item, which is why tax codes are checked at setup.

items.title: Vendor Master Data Setup
items.context: Material Management › Vendor Master Data Setup

cards.title: Purpose of the vendor master setup flow
cards.body:
A vendor card is created first, then its locations with city, tax registration and accounts, and then its contact persons.
Purchasing and master data owners use this flow before a vendor can be invited to quote or receive orders.
Every commercial document then points to one verified supplier record.

cards.title: Vendor setup sequence and downstream dependencies
cards.body:
Cities must exist before locations, because a location's state and country follow from its city.
Currencies and exchange rates support foreign vendors.
Each vendor location carries its own address and tax registration, and orders, quotations and receipts are always placed on a specific location, not only on the vendor.
Contact persons let buyers route requests and follow-ups, and vendor categories map cities to supply sources such as local or open supply for planning.

items.title: Procure-to-Pay (PO Flow)
items.context: Material Management › Procure-to-Pay (PO Flow)

cards.title: Purpose of the procure-to-pay flow
cards.body:
Procure-to-pay turns an internal need into a purchase order on an approved vendor and then into received goods.
Department requesters raise the need, purchase officers source and order, and purchase managers authorise.
Every purchase is backed by recorded demand, competitive offers and an authorised order.

cards.title: Steps from material request to purchase order
cards.body:
Purchase organizations and sub group approved vendors are set up first.
A material request records a department's need; what the store cannot meet becomes a purchase request, checked against budget.
The buyer sends a request for quotation to selected vendors, records their quotations and compares them on a comparative statement.
Booked offers become a purchase order, which is authorised before goods are received at the gate and recorded on a receipt note.

cards.title: How open balances prevent double sourcing and over-ordering
cards.body:
Each document consumes the open balance of the one before it.
A purchase request line already placed on another request for quotation or order is not offered again, so demand is never sourced twice.
A request for quotation is marked partly quoted or completed as vendors respond, and only authorised quotations at their latest revision reach the comparison.
Order quantities cannot exceed the open booking, agreement or request balance they come from, and budgets are checked again on the order.
Receipts then reduce the order balance, so ordered, received and pending quantities always reconcile back to the original request, and buyers can see at any point what is still pending.

items.title: Sourcing and Rate Agreements
items.context: Material Management › Sourcing and Rate Agreements

cards.title: Purpose of sourcing and rate agreements
cards.body:
This flow keeps vendor offers current and turns good offers into rate agreements that later orders can draw on.
Buyers revise quotations, study comparative offers, identify items worth contracting and record material agreements.
Repeat purchases then use agreed rates instead of being re-quoted each time.

cards.title: How offers become agreements and stay valid
cards.body:
A vendor's changed offer after authorisation is recorded as a revised quotation, and only the latest authorised revision is used.
A comparative study prepares a version of the comparison that can be circulated, and items regularly consumed but not yet contracted are listed for rate contract planning.
A material agreement then fixes rates, quantities or values for a period, either directly or from an authorised quotation.
When the period must be extended or shortened, the validity change form adjusts it without re-entering the agreement.

items.title: Purchase Order Lifecycle
items.context: Material Management › Purchase Order Lifecycle

cards.title: What happens to a purchase order after authorisation
cards.body:
Once a purchase order is authorised it is managed through amendments, delivery follow-ups, supplier advances and bank guarantees.
Buyers and purchase managers use these forms until the order is fully received or closed.
The order stays current and controlled without editing the authorised original.

cards.title: Controls on amendments, follow-ups, advances and guarantees
cards.body:
Commercial changes are made on a numbered amendment, which replaces the live order only when authorised.
Follow-ups record each supplier contact and move the schedule date on the latest amendment.
Supplier advance requests are raised against authorised orders when a down-payment term in the payment terms falls due.
Bank guarantee mapping ties a vendor's guarantee to the orders and agreements it secures, and once a guarantee exists the order can no longer be deleted.

items.title: Freight Orders
items.context: Material Management › Freight Orders

cards.title: Purpose of the freight order flow
cards.body:
Freight orders fix transport rates with transporters for inward and outward movements.
Logistics and purchase staff raise them, amend them when terms change, and map them to the orders they cover.
Agreed freight then flows into landed cost instead of being estimated on each order.

cards.title: Freight order, amendment and mapping in sequence
cards.body:
A freight order records transporters, items, routes and rates and is authorised before use.
Changes to terms go through a freight order amendment, which becomes the current version once authorised.
Freight order mapping extends coverage to more purchase, service or sales orders without changing the agreed terms.
A purchase order leg links either to a freight amount or to an agreed freight order, never both, and the freight cost feeds each line's landed rate.

items.title: Goods Receipt and Quality Inspection
items.context: Material Management › Goods Receipt and Quality Inspection

cards.title: Purpose of the goods receipt and inspection flow
cards.body:
This flow records goods arriving at the gate, receives them into a warehouse and inspects them before they become usable stock.
Security, storekeepers and quality controllers each own one step.
Only accepted material enters stock, and rejections are documented for vendor follow-up.

cards.title: Steps from gate entry to accepted stock
cards.body:
QC parameters, quality parameters and specifications are defined first, with group and sub group defaults.
Gate entry records the vehicle and documents at the gate, and the receipt note records quantities against the order.
An inspection intimation sends the received lots for inspection.
The inspection entry records accepted and rejected quantities and parameter readings, and the receipt note is authorised only after inspection is complete.

cards.title: How inspection results decide stock quantity and value
cards.body:
Received quantity is split into accepted, rejected, free-of-charge and replaceable portions on the receipt note.
Inspection can only accept up to the received quantity, and any rejection needs a reason so the vendor can be charged back or asked to replace.
Quality parameters with deductions can reduce the payable price or quantity when results fall outside tolerance.
Only accepted quantity is valued and added to stock, and the receipt then reduces the purchase order balance.
The resulting valued receipt is what finance matches against the purchase bill.
Rejected quantity stays outside stock and is traced through returns or replacements, so the vendor account and stock records agree on what was really delivered and paid for.

items.title: Gate Operations
items.context: Material Management › Gate Operations

cards.title: Purpose of gate operations
cards.body:
Gate operations record every material and vehicle movement through the factory gate that is not a normal purchase receipt.
Security staff record gate passes for material going out or coming in, and vehicle gate in and gate out for loading vehicles.
The company has a dated record of what and who entered or left the premises.

cards.title: How gate passes and vehicle records link together
cards.body:
A gate pass out sends material out, returnable or not, and a gate pass in brings returnable material back against its outstanding balance.
A vehicle gate in records an arriving loading vehicle, optionally against a dispatch advice, and blacklisted vehicles are refused.
Corrections to customer location, agent and items use the gate in amendment until weighment is final.
Vehicle gate out closes the visit, records the invoices carried and cannot be earlier than the gate in time.

items.title: Inventory Storage and Issue
items.context: Material Management › Inventory Storage and Issue

cards.title: Purpose of the storage and issue flow
cards.body:
Warehouses and bins hold stock, and material is issued from them against requests, orders and cost centers.
Storekeepers issue material and take back unused or excess quantities.
Consumption is charged to the right cost center at the right value.

cards.title: Storage setup, issue and return in sequence
cards.body:
Warehouses are defined first, then bins, and sub group settings decide whether items are bin managed.
A material issue reduces stock lot by lot, either directly or against a material request, maintenance order or subcontract order.
Raw material issue covers production consumption by item group.
A material return brings material back within the allowed period at the original issue value, reversing the consumption.

cards.title: How lot-wise stock keeps issue and return values consistent
cards.body:
Stock is held in lots, each with its own receipt rate, stock nature and ownership.
An issue allocates quantity from available lots and carries their value to the department, cost center and account.
Issue type, such as revenue, capital or repairable, decides how that cost is treated in finance.
A return against an issue reverses the same value, while a direct return needs its own rate.
Because every movement is lot-based, stock value, consumption cost and the ledger stay aligned without manual revaluation.
It also means stock reports by warehouse, lot and stock nature always add up to the stock value held in the accounts.

items.title: Stock Transfer
items.context: Material Management › Stock Transfer

cards.title: Purpose of the stock transfer flow
cards.body:
Stock transfers move stock lots between warehouses, divisions or group companies, and adjust value differences after multi-leg moves.
Storekeepers raise transfers, and finance relies on the adjustment to settle transit gains and losses.
Stock and its value stay correct at both ends of every movement.

cards.title: Transfer types, receipts and adjustments
cards.body:
A stock transfer issues from specific lots; one-step transfers also receive, while two-step transfers are received later on a receipt note.
An inter-unit transfer moves stock to another group company in a single document with inter-company entries.
After a multi-leg route is closed, the quantity and value adjustment compares what left with what arrived.
The adjustment revalues received lots and posts any loss in transit.

items.title: Stock Adjustment and Opening
items.context: Material Management › Stock Adjustment and Opening

cards.title: Purpose of stock opening and adjustment
cards.body:
This flow sets opening stock, verifies physical stock and corrects quantity, value, stock nature and reservations.
Storekeepers and inventory controllers use it at go-live, at physical counts and whenever book stock needs correcting.
Book stock, lot balances and stock value then match reality.

cards.title: From opening stock to verified and corrected stock
cards.body:
Opening stock is entered one item at a time or for many items together, with lot details.
A physical stock verification records counted against book quantities and must be authorised.
A stock adjustment then books excess and shortage from the verification, and a value adjustment changes lot value without changing quantity.
Stock nature changes and stock allocation changes reclassify or re-reserve lots with a reason and approval.

items.title: Indent and Budget
items.context: Material Management › Indent and Budget

cards.title: Purpose of budgets and indent defaults
cards.body:
Budgets set approved spending limits, and indent default settings supply the header values used for automatically generated requests.
Management fixes budgets, and planners maintain the defaults for each procurement unit.
Requests and orders are checked against agreed limits and carry consistent values.

cards.title: How budgets are set, amended and enforced
cards.body:
A budget is created by division and department, sub group and item, or cost center for a validity period, and periods cannot overlap.
Changes go through a budget amendment so the original limit stays on record.
Purchase requests and orders consume the budget, and an overrun either blocks or warns depending on company settings.
Indent defaults give automatic requests their warehouse, cost center, department and number series.

items.title: Material Planning and Replenishment
items.context: Material Management › Material Planning and Replenishment

cards.title: Purpose of material planning and replenishment
cards.body:
Material planning decides how much of each item to hold and when to reorder, and then raises requests and release orders automatically.
Planners set it up per procurement unit and keep it current as consumption and suppliers change.
Routine items are replenished on time without manual requests.

cards.title: Planning setup sequence up to automatic replenishment
cards.body:
Procurement units group companies that plan and buy together, with one execution unit.
Each critical item gets a planning type and either min-max or reorder levels, or a consumption pattern built from history.
Supply source, lead days and safety days complete the pattern, and go-ahead live makes the values effective from a date.
Scheduled jobs then raise purchase requests for items below planned levels, and release orders are generated against existing rate contracts.

cards.title: How consumption, lead time and safety days drive reorder figures
cards.body:
The daily consumption rate comes from an authorised consumption pattern based on past usage.
The supply source, local or open, sets the standard lead days and safety days for the item.
Reorder point is lead days plus safety days, multiplied by the consumption rate, and maximum stock adds the reorder quantity on top.
Unit rounding settings decide whether automatic quantities are rounded up to whole units.
Only after go-ahead live do these figures drive the automatic indent job, so planners can review every change before it affects purchasing.
Changing a single item's source or rate later is done through a change of consumption pattern, which recalculates the same figures without repeating the full analysis.

items.title: Service and Subcontract Procurement
items.context: Material Management › Service and Subcontract Procurement

cards.title: Purpose of service and subcontract procurement
cards.body:
This flow buys services, conversion jobs and activities from vendors, mirroring the material purchase flow.
Requesters raise service needs, buyers source and order them, and stores record work done and material returned.
Subcontract work is ordered, tracked and received with the same control as material purchases.

cards.title: Steps from service request to service receipt
cards.body:
A service request records the need, and a service request for quotation invites vendors.
Service quotations, and their revisions, capture offers, and a service agreement can fix rates for a period.
A service order places the work, with input material going out and output expected back, and changes go through a service order amendment.
A bill of quantity breaks the work into measurable items, and the service receipt note records completed work and returned material.

cards.title: How material sent to and returned from subcontractors is tracked
cards.body:
A service order defines the sequence of operations, with an issuable input at the start and a primary output at the end.
Input material leaves stores against the order, and the order controls how much may be sent.
The service receipt note records accepted, rejected and free quantities against one or more orders and brings accepted output into stock.
Order balances drop with each receipt, and an accrual voucher is proposed for the service value.
This keeps material held at vendors visible until it comes back as finished output or is accounted for, and lets buyers chase vendors for anything still outstanding.

items.title: Unit Master
items.context: Material Management › Material Master Data Setup › Unit Master

cards.title: Why units of measure are governed centrally
cards.body:
The Unit Master maintains the units of measure used across the application, such as kilograms, litres or pieces.
Material master administrators add units, record conversions between units, and tell sub groups which unit to use for stock, purchase, sales or production.
Quantities stay consistent across documents, and the right GST unit codes appear on tax returns.

cards.title: Unit conversions and assigning units to sub groups
cards.body:
Unit name and alias must be filled and unique, and a category must be chosen.
A conversion line needs a conversion type, a non-zero unit value, a non-zero conversion value and a target unit, which cannot repeat or be the unit itself.
Every conversion is also stored in reverse for the other unit, so both directions are available.
Sub group assignments need a unit type and cannot repeat a sub group, and a GST unit quantity code is optional.

items.title: Single Field Master
items.context: Material Management › Material Master Data Setup › Single Field Master

cards.title: What the Single Field Master maintains
cards.body:
The Single Field Master is one common master that maintains many simple code-and-name lists, such as locations, technical grades, material categories, quality parameter types, issue labels and vendor groups.
Master data administrators add values whenever a new list entry is needed in transactions or other masters.
All simple lists follow the same entry, duplicate-check, authorisation and company-availability behaviour.

cards.title: Automatic codes, duplicate checks and company availability
cards.body:
When no code is supplied, a code is generated from the list's prefix and the next four-digit running number, and it is kept when the entry is modified.
The name must be unique among entries available to the current company; some lists, such as vendor groups and request types, check uniqueness across all companies.
A new entry is made available to all companies as active, and entries saved in authorised status record the authoriser.
Only lists configured with a default flag allow a default value, and only one default per company is permitted.

items.title: Material Group
items.context: Material Management › Material Master Data Setup › Material Group

cards.title: What a Material Group represents
cards.body:
A Material Group is the second level of the material classification: Category, then Group, then Sub Group, then Item.
Material master administrators create groups when a new family of materials is introduced under an existing category.
Each group has a short code unique within its category, and that code forms part of every item's full code.

cards.title: Group codes, unique names and default quality parameters
cards.body:
A group must belong to a category, and its name and code must be unique within that category.
The displayed group code is the category code followed by the group code.
A group can hold default quality parameters, each needing a non-zero standard value, a tolerance, a deduction rate and a deduction type, with a double deduction threshold when double deduction applies.
These quality defaults flow to sub groups created under the group.

cards.title: How editing a group re-codes every item beneath it
cards.body:
An item's full code is built from category code, group code, sub group code and item code.
When an existing group is saved, the full code of every item under that group is rebuilt, so a corrected group code immediately cascades across the item master.
This guarantees consistent coding but can affect reports, labels and integrations that rely on full codes, so changes need planning.
Quality defaults defined at group level are inherited when sub groups are set up, so a change to a parameter's tolerance or deduction rule influences how future receipts are evaluated.
Validation stops at the first failure in a fixed order: category, code length, name uniqueness, code uniqueness, blank name and then quality lines.

items.title: Material Sub Group
items.context: Material Management › Material Master Data Setup › Material Sub Group

cards.title: What a Material Sub Group controls
cards.body:
A Material Sub Group is the third level of material classification, directly above the item.
Material master administrators create sub groups when a new family of items is introduced under a group or its defaults change.
Each sub group carries tax, unit, warehouse, approved make, approved supplier and bin defaults inherited by every item created under it.

cards.title: Approved suppliers, makes, units and warehouses on a sub group
cards.body:
The sub group's name and code must be unique, and its displayed code is category code plus group code plus sub group code.
Only supplier vendors can be approved; each supplier needs a location and a vendor and location pair can appear only once.
A make can be listed only once, and units are kept as one line per unit type.
Warehouses and bins are optional, with bins kept only when the sub group is bin-managed, and an HSN or SAC code shows its GST rates.

cards.title: How sub group settings govern purchasing, receipt, quality and storage
cards.body:
The sub group is the anchor shared by five business flows: material master setup, procure-to-pay, GST determination, goods receipt with quality inspection, and storage.
Its approved suppliers and makes define who items in the family are normally bought from and under which brands.
Quality parameters are loaded from the parent group and validated the same way, so receipt inspection uses consistent standards and deductions.
Receipt and shipment tolerances, GST category, HSN code, stock unit, warehouses and bin applicability are copied into each new item, determining tolerance checks at the gate and receipt, tax on orders and where stock is kept.
Because items inherit these values at creation, changing a sub group affects new items, so existing items need separate review.

items.title: Make Master
items.context: Material Management › Material Master Data Setup › Make Master

cards.title: Role of the Make Master
cards.body:
The Make Master maintains the central list of manufacturer makes or brands used to describe items, each with a system code.
Material master administrators add makes when a new brand is introduced or a make name needs correcting.
One consistent make list across all companies lets items and transactions be analysed by make.

cards.title: How makes are governed and linked to items
cards.body:
A make is created once and can be linked to the items supplied under that brand.
Make names must be unique, preventing near-duplicate brands across companies.
Makes flagged as tyre makes are available to tyre management only when that function is enabled for the company.
Purchase documents, receipts and issues check that the make chosen on a line is linked to the item, so missing links are discovered during transactions.

items.title: Chapter Heading
items.context: Material Management › Material Master Data Setup › Chapter Heading

cards.title: What the Chapter Heading master holds
cards.body:
The Chapter Heading master lists the tariff chapter headings under which items are classified for excise and customs, and the items belonging to each heading.
Material master and tax administrators maintain it when a new heading is needed or items are reclassified.
It ensures items carry the correct statutory classification on purchase documents.

cards.title: How items are linked to a chapter heading
cards.body:
Only authorised, active items of the current company can be linked to a heading.
On saving, all existing item links of the heading are removed and the currently selected items are written again, so the saved list always reflects the latest selection.
Purchase orders check that the ordered item is linked to a chapter heading, so a missing link surfaces when buying.
Headings can be created, edited, searched and deleted like any master.

items.title: HSN SAC Master
items.context: Material Management › Material Master Data Setup › HSN SAC Master

cards.title: Purpose of the HSN SAC Master under GST
cards.body:
The HSN SAC Master maintains HSN codes for goods and SAC codes for services used under GST.
Tax administrators add codes when new classifications are needed, rates change or items are reclassified.
Each code carries default GST rates and the items assigned to it, so purchase documents pick up the right tax classification.

cards.title: Default GST rates and assigning items to a code
cards.body:
A code can carry default CGST, SGST, IGST and UTGST charges, each chosen from the matching tax group; all are optional.
An optional chapter reference can be recorded for the code.
Items active in the current company are assigned to the code; on saving, all previous item links are replaced by the current selection.
Purchase orders warn when ordered items have no HSN or SAC code, so complete assignment avoids tax errors downstream.

items.title: Technical Specification Head Master
items.context: Material Management › Material Master Data Setup › Technical Specification Head Master

cards.title: What a Technical Specification Head records
cards.body:
The Technical Specification Head Master maintains named technical attributes, such as a dimension or property, grouped under a specification category.
Material master administrators add heads when a new attribute is introduced or its item coverage changes.
Specifications are then captured consistently for the items each head applies to.

cards.title: Categories and item coverage of a specification head
cards.body:
Only specification categories active in the current company can be chosen.
At least one item must be covered by the head; saving replaces the earlier item links with the current selection.
Items offered are active items of the company, with already linked items listed first.
Head names follow the master uniqueness rules, so the same attribute is not created twice.

items.title: Item Master
items.context: Material Management › Material Master Data Setup › Item Master

cards.title: Why the Item Master is the single source of material definitions
cards.body:
The Item Master is the centrally governed definition of every raw material, consumable, spare, service and finished good used in purchasing, stores, production and sales.
Material master administrators create items when the business starts handling a new material or when a Material Master Request is approved.
It prevents duplicate items and supplies the units, tax codes, tolerances, warehouses and accounting rules that every transaction uses.

cards.title: How items sit in the Category, Group and Sub Group hierarchy
cards.body:
Every item is classified under a category, a material group and a material sub group.
Groups are offered for the chosen category and sub groups for the chosen group, limited to active, authorised records of the company.
Choosing a sub group proposes the next free four-digit item code within that sub group, which the user may overwrite.

cards.title: Defaults inherited from the sub group and GST classification
cards.body:
Selecting a sub group loads receipt and shipment tolerances, GST category, HSN or SAC code, bin applicability, stock unit, units of measure, makes, warehouses, vendors, bins and quality parameters.
Where GST applies, a GST category is mandatory, and the chosen HSN or SAC code fills the CGST, SGST, IGST and UTGST rates.
At least one warehouse must be mapped unless the item is a service, and each mapped vendor needs a location.
Tyre items must maintain serial numbers.

cards.title: Unit conversions, dimensions, accounting inheritance and request closure
cards.body:
The stock unit is always the base conversion with a factor of one and cannot be edited; further units carry their own conversion values, and a secondary unit and its conversion value must be given together.
When an item maintains dimensions, a measurement, a non-zero unit weight and a measurement unit are required, and stock is then managed dimension-wise.
On creation, the sub group's item accounting rules are copied to the item, with trading-specific account types copied only for trading material types, and the sub group's technical grades are assigned on every save.
Production lead time and planning strategies are kept only for intermediate and finished goods.
An item created from a Material Master Request marks the request completed and links it; deleting that item reopens the request.
Copying an existing item duplicates its details and mappings except the codes, so new items inherit proven setups without creating duplicates.

items.title: Item Tech Grade Mapping
items.context: Material Management › Material Master Data Setup › Item Tech Grade Mapping

cards.title: Why technical grades are mapped to items
cards.body:
Item Tech Grade Mapping records which technical grades apply to an item or to a whole item sub group.
Material master administrators maintain it when an item or sub group is introduced or its permitted grades change.
Grade selection on item documents can then be limited to valid grades.

cards.title: Mapping at item or sub group level and propagation to items
cards.body:
Grades can be mapped either at item level or at sub group level.
Only active technical grades are offered, at least one grade is required, and each item or sub group and grade pair must be unique.
Items listed are active items of the company, and sub groups listed are authorised and active.
A grade mapped to a sub group is written to the sub group and to every item belonging to it, so whole families inherit the same grades.

items.title: Attribute Standard Value
items.context: Material Management › Material Master Data Setup › Attribute Standard Value

cards.title: What Attribute Standard Value defines
cards.body:
Attribute Standard Value defines the allowed values of item attributes such as size, grade or colour, for a whole sub group or a single item.
Material master administrators use it when an item or sub group with attributes is set up, or a new size, grade or variant is introduced.
Variant lists stay controlled and consistent instead of relying on free-text descriptions.

cards.title: Attribute values, base values and generated variant combinations
cards.body:
Only attributes linked to the chosen sub group or item are offered, every attribute line needs a value, and the same attribute and value cannot repeat.
When generating all combinations, each attribute must have exactly one base value, and combinations are built from every mix of one value per attribute.
A combination whose values are all base values is the base variant and is always active.
Each full generation creates a new version, and existing combinations keep their identity and active status.

items.title: Item Change Unit Weight
items.context: Material Management › Material Master Data Setup › Item Change Unit Weight

cards.title: When to use Item Change Unit Weight
cards.body:
Item Change Unit Weight corrects an existing item's weight, dimension and production unit settings without reopening the full item master.
Material master administrators use it when a unit weight, measurement or production unit conversion was set wrongly or has changed.
Correct values keep weight and quantity conversions right in later transactions.

cards.title: Rules for dimensions, conversions and the change history
cards.body:
When the item maintains dimensions, a measurement and a unit weight are both required.
Each conversion line with a unit needs a conversion type and a non-zero unit value, and the conversion formula is limited to the chosen measurement.
Saving overwrites the item's weight and measurement settings and rebuilds its unit conversions.
Every save also creates a change record with the user and time, while the related bills of material are shown for reference only.

items.title: City Master
items.context: Material Management › Vendor Master Data Setup › City Master

cards.title: Role of the City Master in addresses
cards.body:
The City Master keeps a coded list of cities under their states and countries, with an optional district hierarchy.
Master data administrators add or correct cities when an address needs one that does not exist.
Clean geography prevents duplicate cities across vendor, customer and company addresses and reporting.

cards.title: Country, state and district rules and automatic locations
cards.body:
Only countries and authorised states available in the company are offered, and states are limited to the chosen country.
A city can be flagged as a district, and other cities can be linked to a district city of the same state.
Inactive countries and states appear only when they already belong to the city being edited.
After saving, if no location is linked to the city and none has the same name, a location named after the city is created automatically.

items.title: Vendor Card
items.context: Material Management › Vendor Master Data Setup › Vendor Card

cards.title: Why every business partner starts as a Vendor Card
cards.body:
The Vendor Card is the central party master for suppliers, customers, transporters, agents, contractors and group companies, each with a primary location.
Purchase and accounts officers create cards for new partners or from an approved vendor master request.
Purchasing, sales and finance documents pick parties from this one governed list with validated tax data.

cards.title: Party type, GST registration and commercial fields
cards.body:
Payment terms, tax group and terms group apply only to customers, suppliers and contractors, with sales terms for customers and purchase terms otherwise.
The GST registration type decides whether a GST number and applicable date are needed; unregistered and foreign parties have no GST number.
MSME number is mandatory when the party is MSME registered.
Bank lines need branch and account number, only contacts with a name are saved, and a vendor may have only one default billed-to and one default consignee location.

cards.title: Automatic ledger accounts and converting vendor master requests
cards.body:
When a new party is created, one ledger account is created for each account mapping of its party type, named after the party with the mapped suffix, along with group mappings and an account rule linked to the location.
A ledger name duplicating an existing account in the same chart is refused, and no accounts are created when a party is modified.
Only approved vendor master requests of the company or its head office, not yet linked, can be converted; the party name and full address must match the request, which is then linked and marked converted.
Configurable completeness checks can warn or block when contacts, banks, PAN or other details are missing.
All writes of one save succeed or fail together, preventing half-created parties without accounts.

items.title: Location Detail
items.context: Material Management › Vendor Master Data Setup › Location Detail

cards.title: Why each partner address is a Location Detail
cards.body:
Location Detail maintains every address at which the company deals with a business partner, with the statutory and commercial data that applies there.
It is used when a partner opens a new branch, warehouse or billing address, when registrations change, or when an approved request asks for a new location.
Transactions carry the correct address, GST state, registration, payment terms and bank details.

cards.title: GST registration checks at each location
cards.body:
For registered GST types, the state must have a GST state code and the PAN is mandatory with exactly ten characters.
A GSTIN or UIN is required, and a GSTIN must be fifteen characters containing the state code followed by the PAN.
Unregistered and foreign locations carry no GSTIN, and the GST applicable date is kept only for registered, PSU and composition types.
Only one location per partner can be the default billed-to, and one the default consignee.

cards.title: Account rule inheritance, request linking and configurable completeness
cards.body:
When a new location is created, the account rules held by the partner's other locations are copied to it, so postings for the new address follow the same ledger mapping.
Only open vendor-location requests of the company or its subsidiaries can be used; the partner name and full address must match the request, which is then linked and closed, and deleting the location reopens it.
Configurable checks can require MSME registration, phone, e-mail, PAN, contacts and bank accounts, as warnings or hard stops.
Divisions can be linked when the partner is a group company with divisions.
Copying from another location brings its contacts and bank accounts as new records under the selected partner.

items.title: Vendor Contact Person
items.context: Material Management › Vendor Master Data Setup › Vendor Contact Person

cards.title: Purpose of Vendor Contact Person records
cards.body:
Vendor Contact Person records the people to contact at each vendor location, with their contact details.
Purchase officers maintain it when a vendor location is set up or its staff changes.
Purchasing and accounts staff always know whom to contact, and contacts can be chosen on quotations and orders.

cards.title: How contact details are captured
cards.body:
Choosing a city fills the state and country, and choosing a state fills the country, keeping addresses consistent.
The full address is composed from address lines, city, state and country.
Designation can reuse designations already recorded on other contacts.
Phone, mobile, fax and e-mail are optional, and birth and anniversary dates are saved only when entered.
Accurate contacts let buyers route quotation requests and order follow-ups to the right person.

items.title: Vendor Category
items.context: Material Management › Vendor Master Data Setup › Vendor Category

cards.title: What Vendor Category maps for planning
cards.body:
Vendor Category assigns cities to a vendor source, such as local supply, open supply, government or foreign.
Planners use it to define which cities count as local or open market.
Purchase history can then be split by source type without tagging every vendor individually.

cards.title: Assigning cities to vendor sources
cards.body:
Cities are assigned to a chosen vendor source by selection, and only the city selection can be changed.
A city can belong to only one source, so cities already mapped to another source are not offered.
Supply source suggestions in planning use this mapping to decide whether past orders went to local or non-local cities.
Keeping the mapping accurate therefore directly affects suggested sources and the standard lead and safety days applied.

items.title: Purchase Organization
items.context: Material Management › Procure-to-Pay (PO Flow) › Purchase Organization

cards.title: What a Purchase Organization represents
cards.body:
A Purchase Organization is a named buying unit grouping one or more companies, and divisions where they apply, with one executing unit.
Purchase managers set it up when procurement is organised across units or membership changes.
It is the first step of procure-to-pay, giving each unit a clear buying organisation.

cards.title: Membership and execution rules for purchase organizations
cards.body:
At least one member company must be selected, and only selected members are saved.
A company or division already belonging to another purchase organization is not offered, so each unit belongs to exactly one organization.
Divisions are listed only when the company works with divisions.
Exactly one member must be marked as the execution unit that carries out purchasing for the organization.

items.title: Material Request
items.context: Material Management › Procure-to-Pay (PO Flow) › Material Request

cards.title: What a Material Request represents
cards.body:
A Material Request is a department's internal request for stock items, either to be issued from the store or as the first step towards buying.
Department requesters and storekeepers use it, and maintenance orders can also raise requests for their required items.
Demand is recorded once, approved through its status and traced to the issue or purchase request that fulfils it.

cards.title: Line, cost center and issue details on a Material Request
cards.body:
At least one line needs an item; only active, inventory-managed, non-service items held in a warehouse are offered, and each line needs a unit and a required quantity above zero.
Makes, units and technical grades are limited to those linked to the item, and mandatory quality parameters must be filled.
Where cost centers are used every line needs one, and a header cost center is copied to all lines.
Returnable, chargeable and issue-to details apply only when the request is for material issue, and a return date cannot be before the request date.

cards.title: Requests raised from maintenance orders and service contracts
cards.body:
When the source is not direct, a reference document is mandatory.
For maintenance orders only authorised, open or partly covered orders of the company and division with outstanding item quantity are offered, and each line shows the balance not yet requested on other requests.
Requesting more than that balance raises a warning so the requester must consciously confirm over-demand.
For annual maintenance contracts, each item and make must belong to the contract and a header cost center is mandatory.
Capital requests with non-capital items are warned, schedules are created automatically for the full quantity, and the request moves through Initial, Release and Authorized with user and date stamps.
This keeps maintenance spare demand tied to the work that justified it.

items.title: Purchase Request
items.context: Material Management › Procure-to-Pay (PO Flow) › Purchase Request

cards.title: Role of the Purchase Request (Indent) in procurement
cards.body:
The Purchase Request, also called the indent, is a department's formal, priced request to buy stock items.
Department requesters raise it directly or to fulfil a Material Request or material plan, and purchase officers later convert it into orders.
Procurement starts only from an approved, budget-checked demand recorded on this document.

cards.title: Line requirements, sources and default rates on a Purchase Request
cards.body:
A source document is mandatory: direct requests allow free item entry, while requests from a Material Request take type, department and requester from it and default quantities to the outstanding balance.
Every line needs a unit, a required quantity and an indent quantity above zero, and a rate above zero that defaults to the latest purchase order rate.
Cost center is mandatory per line where the company uses cost centers, and mandatory quality parameters need values.
Net amount, the sum of line amounts, must be above zero, and the department must belong to the selected division.

cards.title: Budget control and multi-level approval of purchase requests
cards.body:
Each request is checked against authorised budgets valid on its date at four levels: the division total, the department total, each item's line amount and each cost center's total.
An overrun shows the remaining budget and blocks the request only when the company's budget validation is switched on.
Capital requests containing non-capital items raise a warning, while capital items on a non-capital request are refused.
Where multi-level authorisation is configured, the approval route is saved with the request, notifications go to the next approver, and the status cannot be set to Authorized directly until the last level approves.
Reserved lines must carry reservation detail whose quantities equal the indent quantity, and the original releaser is preserved when a released request is updated.
Once authorised the request is locked, and each line's status follows the header.

items.title: Request for Quotation
items.context: Material Management › Procure-to-Pay (PO Flow) › Request for Quotation

cards.title: Why buyers issue a Request for Quotation
cards.body:
A Request for Quotation is a formal, numbered invitation to selected vendors to quote for a defined list of materials, quantities and delivery dates.
Purchase officers raise it from authorised purchase requests, project requirements, sales orders or a direct need.
Every vendor receives the same specification and deadlines, and quotations can be traced back to one request.

cards.title: Date sequence, item lines and vendor selection rules
cards.body:
Submission date cannot precede the request date, opening and validity dates cannot precede submission, and opening cannot be after validity.
Item and make must be unique, and each item needs a unit, a non-zero quantity and a delivery date not before the request date.
Vendors can be chosen from all approved suppliers, from item-vendor mappings or from a vendor group; at least one vendor is required, each with a location, and no vendor and location may repeat.
Source lines of the same item and make must use the same request unit.

cards.title: Reserving purchase request lines and consolidating demand
cards.body:
For purchase request sources, only authorised requests of the company and division, or of companies in the same purchase organisation where this company executes buying, are offered.
A request line must still be open and not already on another request for quotation or purchase order for the same item, make and grade, so demand is never sourced twice.
Selected source lines are consolidated into one line per item, make and unit with summed quantity, earliest schedule as delivery date and copied tax codes and specifications.
Unit conversions from request to quotation units use the item's conversion factors.
Each saved link recalculates the purchase request's ordered quantity and status, keeping requirement tracking accurate.
Output is produced separately for each invited vendor.

items.title: Quotation
items.context: Material Management › Procure-to-Pay (PO Flow) › Quotation

cards.title: Purpose of recording a vendor Quotation
cards.body:
A Quotation records a vendor's priced offer, with taxes, delivery days and terms, against an authorised Request for Quotation.
Purchase officers enter it when an invited vendor submits its offer.
Offers are captured in one structured format per request, enabling comparison, booking and ordering at the quoted rates.

cards.title: Eligible requests, invited vendors and mandatory offer details
cards.body:
Only authorised requests that are open or partly quoted and still have an invited vendor location without a quotation are offered.
The vendor and location must be among those invited, and only one quotation is allowed per request, vendor and location.
The vendor quotation number and date are mandatory; the date cannot be after the entry date or before the request date, and validity cannot precede the entry date.
Each selected item needs a non-zero quantity, a non-zero rate and delivery days, plus freight type and payment mode.

cards.title: How quotations close the request and feed the comparative statement
cards.body:
Line amount is quantity times rate, and taxes are captured per item and make so the comparison can work on landed rates.
After each save, the request is marked completed when every invited vendor location has quoted; otherwise it is marked partly quoted.
Only authorised quotations, at their latest revision, are compared on the comparative statement, and only open quotation items can be booked.
If a vendor changes its offer after authorisation, a Revised Quotation must be used, so the original offer stays on record and bookings remain protected.
This chain ensures buying decisions always rest on authorised, traceable offers.

items.title: Comparative Statement
items.context: Material Management › Procure-to-Pay (PO Flow) › Comparative Statement

cards.title: Purpose of the Comparative Statement in vendor selection
cards.body:
The Comparative Statement places all authorised vendor offers for one Request for Quotation side by side.
Purchase officers and managers use it after quotations are entered and authorised to decide which vendor supplies which quantity at which rate.
It documents a transparent selection with prepared, checked and approved signatures, and its bookings feed purchase orders.

cards.title: Which offers are compared and how the landed rate is judged
cards.body:
Offers include the latest authorised revision of each quotation from an invited vendor location, plus valid authorised rate agreements containing the requested items.
For every item the statement shows quoted quantity, rate, delivery date, each tax and charge, total amount, GST and the landed rate, which is total amount less GST.
The lowest landed rate and the earliest delivery are highlighted per item, and terms and conditions are compared head by head.
The last purchase rate and vendor for each item are shown for reference.

cards.title: Booking quantities for purchase orders and the limits on cancelling them
cards.body:
A buyer books a quantity and rate against a chosen offer; one booking exists per request, item, make and offer.
The booking quantity must be above zero, cannot exceed the balance enquiry quantity (requested quantity less what is already booked), and cannot fall below the purchase order quantity already raised on it.
Items from quotations that are no longer open cannot be booked.
After each booking, the total booked quantity is allocated back to the underlying request lines in order, up to each line's quantity.
A booking cannot be cancelled once any purchase order quantity exists for the item; cancellation releases the booked quantity back to the request lines.
Item status is colour-coded as partly booked, fully booked, or fully converted to purchase orders.
The statement itself is read-only, so commercial decisions are captured only through bookings.

items.title: Purchase Order
items.context: Material Management › Procure-to-Pay (PO Flow) › Purchase Order

cards.title: Commercial purpose and role ownership of the Purchase Order
cards.body:
The Purchase Order is the company's commercial commitment to a vendor for items or services at agreed rates, quantities, delivery schedules, freight and payment terms.
Purchase officers draft it from approved purchase requests, quotations, comparative statement bookings or agreements, and purchase managers authorise it.
Purchases are made only against valid demand, approved rates and available budget.

cards.title: Order types, purchase types and allowed reference documents
cards.body:
An order can be a letter of intent, a regular purchase order or a release order, and its purchase type is capital, general or drop-shipment, either domestic or import.
Each document type allows certain references, such as quotations, purchase requests, agreements, sales orders or direct entry.
Changing the document type resets purchase type, category and reference so incompatible combinations cannot be saved.

cards.title: Mandatory commercial terms and entry constraints on purchase orders
cards.body:
Vendor, vendor location, document type, purchase type, category, validity date, pay-to and bill-to parties and payment mode are mandatory, and at least one consignee location is required.
The validity date cannot precede the order date, and the order date cannot precede its reference date.
Every line needs a quantity above zero and an entered rate, and the same item, make and grade cannot repeat.
Capital items are not allowed on general orders, and intermediate or finished goods are blocked except on drop-shipment orders.
CGST and SGST may be used only within a state and IGST only across states.

cards.title: Source balance limits and budget checks on order quantities
cards.body:
Order quantity cannot exceed the open balance of the comparative statement booking, the agreement quantity, amount or schedule, or the purchase request it is drawn from.
Lines of the same item must use the same order unit and rate, and inventory and discrete raw material requests cannot be combined.
Division, department, item and cost center budgets are checked; an overrun blocks the order when the company enforces budget validation, otherwise it is a warning.
Reserved purchase request quantities must be fully allocated to the order quantity.

cards.title: Multi-tier authorisation locking and referential integrity barriers
cards.body:
Purchase orders progress through Initial, Release and Authorized, and every save also writes an amendment copy so the version history is complete.
The approval group is chosen from the order's net amount; under multi-level approval only the final approver can authorise, and approvers must record an action, with a comment for rejection.
A user may authorise only orders whose net amount falls within that user's authorisation limit, and completed or cancelled orders cannot be authorised.
On a released order only members of the approval group may update it, and once authorised the order is locked; later changes require a Purchase Order Amendment.
On authorisation the account assignment is filled automatically and lines without an account name can be warned or blocked.
Deletion is refused once an amendment, a follow-on order from a letter of intent, an advance request or a bank guarantee exists against the order, preserving the commercial audit trail.

cards.title: Transportation routes, freight terms and their effect on landed cost
cards.body:
An order may define a multi-leg transportation route, each leg with transport mode, freight type, from and to locations that differ, warehouse and recipient.
Each leg or header carries either a freight amount or a link to an agreed freight order, never both.
Capital orders cannot define a route, drop-shipment orders disable routes, and discrete items cannot have routes or other expense heads.
When rate validation is used for an order, routes, tax-inclusive charges and more than one item are not allowed.
Other expenses are recorded by expense head, billing location and party, and an expense head already used on a receipt cannot be deleted.
Freight and expenses feed the landed rate of each line, so receipt valuation reflects the full cost of bringing the material in.

items.title: Revised Quotation
items.context: Material Management › Sourcing and Rate Agreements › Revised Quotation

cards.title: When a Revised Quotation is recorded
cards.body:
A Revised Quotation records a vendor's changed offer against an already authorised quotation, as a numbered revision.
It is used when the vendor changes price, terms or quantities after authorisation.
Purchasing orders against the latest authorised offer while earlier offers stay on record.

cards.title: Revision rules and protection of booked quantities
cards.body:
Only the latest authorised revision of an open or partly open quotation can be revised, and the new revision starts from that live offer in Initial status.
Request, vendor, location and the vendor's original number and date are carried over unchanged.
Quantity cannot fall below what is already booked or ordered, and rate cannot change on lines with bookings.
Only an authorised revision replaces the live quotation; an unauthorised revision leaves the live offer untouched.

items.title: Material Comparative Study
items.context: Material Management › Sourcing and Rate Agreements › Material Comparative Study

cards.title: Purpose of the Material Comparative Study
cards.body:
The Material Comparative Study prepares a spreadsheet version of the comparative statement for a Request for Quotation that has received vendor quotations.
Buyers use it when they want to circulate or file the comparison of offers.
It records which requests already have a prepared statement and provides a documented basis for vendor selection.

cards.title: Eligible requests, display levels and the prepared mark
cards.body:
Only requests of the company with at least one quotation and no prepared statement are listed.
The comparison can be shown at item level, document level or as per quotation, with an optional subject line.
Saving stores the subject and display level and marks the request's statement as prepared.
If the Request for Quotation is saved again, the prepared mark is reset so the comparison can be refreshed; terms and custom field options apply only to the export.

items.title: Material Agreement
items.context: Material Management › Sourcing and Rate Agreements › Material Agreement

cards.title: What a Material Agreement establishes with a supplier
cards.body:
A Material Agreement is a rate contract with a supplier location that fixes item rates, quantities or values, commercial terms and taxes for an agreement period.
Purchasing negotiates it directly or on the basis of an authorised quotation.
Purchase orders can then be raised against agreed terms within the validity period while the agreement value is controlled.

cards.title: Agreement types, period and item values
cards.body:
Agreements are by rate, quantity or amount: rate agreements fix only rates, quantity agreements fix rate and quantity, and amount agreements fix only a value.
The period cannot start before the agreement date and must end after it starts.
Line amount is rate times quantity, and agreement value is the sum of selected lines; at least one item is required.
For quotation-based agreements, only the latest authorised quotation revision is offered, item details are locked, and the agreement date cannot precede the quotation date.

cards.title: Recurring schedules, tolerances and how orders consume agreements
cards.body:
Recurring agreements are allowed only for quantity agreements; each item's quantity is spread across schedule periods that must lie inside the agreement period, may not overlap and must total the item quantity.
Automatic scheduling can split quantity equally across monthly, quarterly or yearly periods, with rounding added to the first period.
Quantity agreements may carry plus and minus tolerance, and may allow one alternate item in orders.
Purchase orders cannot exceed the agreement's balance quantity, amount or schedule balance, and order dates must fall within the agreement and schedule periods.
Recurring agreements can also drive supplier advances and bank guarantees.
Changing validity after authorisation requires a formal validity change, protecting orders already placed.

items.title: Material Agreement Validity Change
items.context: Material Management › Sourcing and Rate Agreements › Material Agreement Validity Change

cards.title: Why agreement validity is changed through a formal document
cards.body:
The Material Agreement validity change is an authorised document that changes the start and end dates, and recurring schedule, of a material agreement.
It is used when an agreement is about to expire or must be shortened, extended or re-planned.
Validity changes are approved and traceable, with the old period kept on record, instead of editing an authorised agreement directly.

cards.title: Eligible agreements and limits on the new period
cards.body:
Only active agreements of the company and chosen division are offered, and selecting one fills vendor, current period, items and schedule.
Vendor details, items and the current period are read-only; only the new period and schedule can change.
The new start date cannot be after, and the new end date cannot be before, the latest purchase order raised against the agreement.
A schedule quantity cannot drop below what has already been ordered against it.

cards.title: Recurring schedules and what authorising a validity change does
cards.body:
For recurring agreements, schedule lines must add up to the item quantity, each line needs both dates with the end not before the start, both inside the new period, and schedule periods may not overlap.
Schedule lines are saved only for recurring agreements and only with a non-zero quantity.
On authorisation, the agreement's dates are replaced, the old schedule is retained in the change record marked as old, unused schedule lines are removed and the new ones inserted.
Schedule lines already used by purchase orders are preserved, protecting orders in progress.
Once authorised, the change itself can no longer be modified, and release and authorisation stamp the user and date.

items.title: Items for Rate Contract
items.context: Material Management › Sourcing and Rate Agreements › Items for Rate Contract

cards.title: Purpose of Items for Rate Contract analysis
cards.body:
Items for Rate Contract lists regularly consumed items that are not yet covered by a valid material agreement.
Purchasing uses it when planning annual rate contracts for procurement units that run consumption-based replenishment.
It highlights steady-consumption items with a suggested quantity, value and candidate suppliers.

cards.title: How candidate items, quantities and suppliers are suggested
cards.body:
Candidate items come from the latest planning release of the selected procurement units.
Items already in a material agreement valid today are excluded.
Suggested annual quantity is the consumption rate times 365, and suggested value uses the latest receipt rate net of discount.
Suggested suppliers are vendors that previously received orders for the item, classified as local, foreign or open source, and values are summarised by group and sub group.
The analysis is read-only.

items.title: Purchase Order Amendment
items.context: Material Management › Purchase Order Lifecycle › Purchase Order Amendment

cards.title: Why a Purchase Order Amendment is used instead of editing
cards.body:
A Purchase Order Amendment revises an authorised purchase order through a numbered version with its own date, reason and status.
Buyers raise it when rate, quantity, delivery schedule, tax, freight or payment terms change after the order was released to the vendor.
Order history is preserved version by version, and the live order always reflects the last authorised amendment.

cards.title: Eligible orders, mandatory reason and fixed order identity
cards.body:
Only orders whose latest version is authorised and which are authorised, in progress, or completed and formally re-opened can be amended.
An order with an unauthorised amendment in progress cannot be amended again until that one is authorised or deleted.
A reason is mandatory, and the amendment date must fall within the current financial year and not precede the order date.
Document type, purchase type, category, reference, vendor, location, division and order date are inherited and cannot change, and completed or cancelled orders cannot be amended.

cards.title: Protecting received goods and propagating authorised amendments
cards.body:
Lines already received on a goods receipt cannot be removed, cannot change make or grade, and cannot drop below the received quantity.
Every amended quantity is checked against the comparative statement booking balance, agreement balance by quantity, amount or schedule, and purchase request balance.
Budgets at division, department, item and cost center level are rechecked, and authorisation is allowed only within the approver's monetary limit.
Under multi-level approval an approval group is mandatory, the status cannot be set to Authorized directly, and rejection returns the amendment to Initial.
When authorised, the live order's detail is replaced by the amendment, purchase request quantities are reversed and re-applied, and landed rates, routes, project budgets and contract status are updated; any error cancels the whole save.
GST rules still apply: CGST and SGST only within a state and IGST only across states.

items.title: Purchase Order Follow Up
items.context: Material Management › Purchase Order Lifecycle › Purchase Order Follow Up

cards.title: What Purchase Order Follow Up is for
cards.body:
Purchase Order Follow Up lets a buyer review open delivery schedules of authorised purchase orders and record each contact with the supplier.
Buyers use it when chasing suppliers for pending deliveries, capturing the revised delivery date agreed and a remark.
Order schedules then show the latest committed date, with a dated trail of follow-ups per order line.

cards.title: Which schedules are listed and how revised dates update the order
cards.body:
Lines come from authorised purchase orders of the company dated within the chosen period whose lines are authorised or in progress.
Balance quantity is scheduled quantity less received quantity, with receipts allocated to schedules in date order.
The new schedule date cannot be earlier than the order date or the follow-up date, and at least one line must be selected.
Saving records the follow-up and moves the schedule date on the latest order amendment, and lines are highlighted as due, due within seven days or later.

items.title: Supplier Advance Request
items.context: Material Management › Purchase Order Lifecycle › Supplier Advance Request

cards.title: Why buyers raise a Supplier Advance Request
cards.body:
A Supplier Advance Request asks the company to pay a supplier an advance that is due under the payment terms of an authorised purchase order, service order or material agreement.
It is raised when a down-payment term falls due or when the supplier sends a proforma invoice for an advance.
Every advance stays traceable to the exact order and payment term that allowed it.

cards.title: How the advance amount and the request ceiling are worked out
cards.body:
The advance amount is the payment-term percentage applied to the order's basic value (pay on basic) or net value (pay on net); a pay-on-balance term takes the net value less all other down-payment terms.
Amounts already requested on the same order and term, in any status, are shown as previously requested.
A new request proposes the advance amount less previous requests, and the requested amount can never exceed advance amount minus previous requests plus the allowed tolerance.
Entering a percentage fills the amount and entering an amount fills the percentage.

cards.title: Eligibility, progress conditions and accounting prerequisites for supplier advances
cards.body:
Only authorised source documents qualify: for purchase and service orders the latest authorised amendment is used, and for material agreements only authorised recurring agreements are offered.
The source must belong to the chosen vendor location, match the division and carry a Down Payment or Down Payment against proforma term.
When a term demands a progress percentage, the actual progress, measured as accepted quantity times rate on authorised goods receipts, must reach that percentage before an advance is allowed.
Proforma-based terms require the proforma invoice number and a non-zero proforma amount.
The request date cannot precede the order date, and a request after the order's validity or last schedule date is warned or blocked depending on configuration.
When supplier advance posting is switched on for the company, the order's account assignment must hold a supplier payment account, or a prepayment account where prepayment applies.
Once authorised, the request status is locked.

items.title: Bank Guarantee
items.context: Material Management › Purchase Order Lifecycle › Bank Guarantee

cards.title: What Bank Guarantee mapping achieves in purchasing
cards.body:
The Bank Guarantee mapping ties one vendor bank guarantee to the purchase orders, service orders and agreements it secures.
It is used when a vendor's guarantee is accepted as security for specific orders whose payment mode is the guarantee payment mode.
It shows exactly which documents each guarantee covers and stops the same guarantee balance being used twice.

cards.title: Which guarantees and documents can be linked together
cards.body:
Only guarantees permitted for the logged-in company and division are offered, and a general-purpose guarantee already mapped elsewhere is hidden.
Documents offered belong to the guarantee's vendors, use the guarantee payment mode and sit in the mapping's company and division.
For orders only the latest amendment is offered, and at least one document must be selected.
The mapping date cannot be earlier than the guarantee date, and each document date must fall within the guarantee's validity.

cards.title: Balance-type guarantees and the arithmetic that protects their cover
cards.body:
A balance-type guarantee covers only purchase orders and service orders, while a general guarantee may also cover material and service agreements.
For a balance guarantee, documents already mapped under another guarantee are excluded, and each document must be dated on or after the guarantee date.
The guarantee balance is the guarantee amount less net values mapped elsewhere plus amounts already paid or adjusted against them.
That balance must not fall below the total net value of the selected documents less what has been paid, nor below guarantee amount minus net value plus paid amount.
Totals combine the currently selected documents with documents mapped to the same guarantee in earlier mappings.
These checks ensure the bank cover always matches the unpaid exposure on the orders it secures.

items.title: Freight Order
items.context: Material Management › Freight Orders › Freight Order

cards.title: Why a Freight Order is agreed with a transporter
cards.body:
A Freight Order is a numbered agreement that fixes freight terms with a transporter for a validity period.
It covers chosen items, transporters and orders, for inward purchase and service orders or outward sales orders.
Freight cost is agreed once and reused by orders and freight invoices instead of being negotiated for every movement.

cards.title: Freight rate types, rate basis and validity rules
cards.body:
Without a freight basis, a non-zero freight rate is mandatory; with a basis, rates come from the basis lines by location or distance.
Location lines need different from and to locations and a rate, while distance lines need a valid distance range and a rate.
A per-unit rate requires a unit, and a per-trip rate always calculates on received quantity.
The validity end date cannot precede the start date, and the reference date cannot be after the document date.

cards.title: Shortage tolerance, order coverage and the effect on purchase landed rates
cards.body:
When shortage tolerance applies, a tolerance unit and a deduction basis are required, with at least one range line holding range from, range to and the tolerance allowed.
Transporter lines need a valid location, cannot repeat a transporter, and always include the header transporter.
Covered orders must be purchase or service orders for inward freight and sales orders for outward freight; a routed purchase order needs a valid route, and a sales order needs consignee name and location.
The same order and route cannot appear twice, and an order whose route already carries a freight amount is rejected.
Saving the order list recalculates the landed rate of the linked purchase orders, so freight agreed here flows directly into material costing.
Release and authorisation stamp the user and date.

items.title: Freight Order Amendment
items.context: Material Management › Freight Orders › Freight Order Amendment

cards.title: Purpose of a Freight Order Amendment
cards.body:
A Freight Order Amendment revises an authorised freight order while keeping the earlier version.
It is used when agreed freight terms such as rate, tolerance or validity change after authorisation.
Each revision is traceable instead of overwriting the original terms.

cards.title: Which freight orders can be amended and when changes take effect
cards.body:
Only freight orders whose latest revision is authorised and current, with no pending unauthorised revision, can be amended; the amendment number is the current number plus one.
The amendment date cannot be earlier than the freight order date and must pass back-dating controls.
Only rate, calculation basis, tolerance, validity, tax rule, remarks, basis lines, tolerance lines and terms can be revised; items, orders and transporters are maintained through Freight Order Mapping.
Only an authorised amendment replaces the live freight terms.

items.title: Freight Order Mapping
items.context: Material Management › Freight Orders › Freight Order Mapping

cards.title: What Freight Order Mapping maintains
cards.body:
Freight Order Mapping maintains the items, transporters and orders covered by an already authorised freight order.
It is used when new orders must be covered or the item or transporter list changes after authorisation.
Freight terms stay unchanged while their coverage grows, without raising a new amendment.

cards.title: Rules for adding orders and transporters to a freight order
cards.body:
Only authorised freight orders of the company at their current version can be selected.
Inward freight lists purchase and service orders, outward freight lists sales orders, filtered to the freight order's items and locations.
A routed purchase order needs a valid route, a sales order needs consignee name and location, and the same order and route cannot repeat.
Changing the items re-lists the eligible orders, and the header transporter cannot be removed from the transporter list.

items.title: QC Parameter Master
items.context: Material Management › Goods Receipt and Quality Inspection › QC Parameter Master

cards.title: Purpose of the QC Parameter Master
cards.body:
The QC Parameter Master defines the quality parameters checked on incoming material, such as moisture or purity.
Each parameter carries a unit, standard values, a tolerance and the rules for deducting price or quantity when a result falls outside tolerance.
Quality controllers maintain it so acceptance limits and deductions are uniform across receipts.
