cards.title: Standard values, deduction types and parameter sequence
cards.body:
The first standard value is mandatory and non-zero; a second standard value is optional.
Deduction can be single or double, and a double-deduction threshold is required only for double deduction.
Where deduction details are not used, the system saves standard defaults: deduct on the lower value, by quantity, on the basic rate, as a single deduction.
With lot-wise quality checking each parameter needs a unique sequence, which cannot change once lot quality values exist.

items.title: Quality Parameter
items.context: Material Management › Goods Receipt and Quality Inspection › Quality Parameter

cards.title: What the Quality Parameter catalogue defines
cards.body:
The Quality Parameter catalogue defines the characteristics that quality tests measure, such as moisture or colour, with their format and acceptable values.
Quality controllers maintain it before specifications, tests or inspection plans are defined.
Results are then recorded and judged against one consistent definition of each characteristic.

cards.title: Value formats, ranges, tolerances and standard values
cards.body:
A parameter is numeric, alphanumeric or date; numeric parameters need a reporting length and decimal precision.
Standard values can be fixed, variable or defined as normal values or ranges; range values need both lower and upper limits.
Numeric normal values may carry a tolerance unit with lower and upper tolerance, and only one value can be the default.
Standard values already used by tests, specifications, inspection plans or results cannot be edited or deleted, and when synchronisation is enabled each parameter also creates or updates a matching QC parameter.

items.title: Specification
items.context: Material Management › Goods Receipt and Quality Inspection › Specification

cards.title: What a quality Specification defines
cards.body:
A Specification is a named set of quality parameters with expected values or ranges, applied to items, item sub groups or grades.
Quality controllers create it when a product standard or customer or supplier requirement is agreed.
Inspection then compares results against one agreed standard.

cards.title: Coverage, parameters and the no-overlap rule
cards.body:
At least one item, sub group or grade must be covered at the chosen level, and at least one quality parameter is required, each appearing only once.
Customer-specific specifications need at least one customer location, and supplier-specific ones at least one supplier location.
An item, sub group or grade cannot be covered by two general specifications, and the same customer location and item combination cannot appear in two customer specifications.
Values follow the parameter's definition, and ranges need both limits.

items.title: Gate Entry
items.context: Material Management › Goods Receipt and Quality Inspection › Gate Entry

cards.title: Why every inward vehicle starts with a Gate Entry
cards.body:
Gate Entry records every inward vehicle and consignment arriving at the factory gate before it is received into stores.
Security and gate staff capture the supplier location, the reference documents and the items and quantities declared on the supplier challan.
It is the company's first controlled record of inward material, used later to reconcile receipts, weighment and freight.

cards.title: Reference documents, vehicle details and date checks at the gate
cards.body:
A source document type, vendor and vendor location are mandatory, and for every source other than direct at least one reference document must be selected with at least one of its items.
Reference dates cannot be after the gate entry date, and a purchase order date cannot be after the challan date.
Challan, lorry receipt, weighment slip and e-way bill numbers each require their date, and none of these dates may be later than the gate entry date.
A blacklisted vehicle number cannot be used, and freight type must be selected.

cards.title: Stopping over-supply at the gate and keeping freight consistent
cards.body:
The challan quantity cannot exceed the open balance on the order plus tolerance, where tolerance is a fixed quantity or a percentage of the ordered quantity, unless the order is marked for manual closing.
This limit is applied when quantities are entered, again on saving, and once more for purchase order lines not governed by freight routes.
For subcontract orders, the quantity cannot exceed the balance after material already received through gate passes.
All selected item lines must share the same freight type, route and from-to freight route, and capital and non-capital items cannot be mixed.
When purchase orders carry different exchange rates from the entry's currency rate, the user must confirm before saving.
Status moves from Initial to Release to Authorized with user and date stamps, giving a dependable starting point for the receipt note.

items.title: Material Receipt Note (GRN)
items.context: Material Management › Goods Receipt and Quality Inspection › Material Receipt Note (GRN)

cards.title: Purpose and ownership of the Material Receipt Note (GRN)
cards.body:
The Material Receipt Note records the physical receipt of material at a company warehouse and turns it into usable stock.
Storekeepers prepare it once a consignment has arrived, confirming what was received against the order, gate entry, stock transfer or challan.
It records accepted, rejected, free-of-charge and replaceable quantities and gives finance a valued inward entry for the purchase bill.

cards.title: Where a receipt can come from and how accepted quantity is derived
cards.body:
A receipt can reference a purchase order, a gate entry, a stock transfer, an inter-unit dispatch challan, a sales order or be made directly.
Accepted quantity equals received quantity less rejected and free-of-charge quantity, and the line amount is accepted quantity times rate.
Item, make and rate can be freely entered only for direct receipts; referenced receipts take them from the source document.

cards.title: Everyday receipt checks: quantities, references and supporting documents
cards.body:
Vendor and vendor location are mandatory, at least one item line must be selected, and the same item and make cannot repeat; capital and non-capital items cannot be mixed.
For purchase order and gate entry receipts, accepted plus rejected plus free quantity must equal received quantity, or challan quantity where the company receives on challan.
Selected references must share source type and currency, and a gate entry already used by another receipt is refused.
Vendor bill number and date go together, and challan, lorry receipt and e-way bill dates cannot be after the receipt date.
Batch items need a batch number and expiry-tracked items need an expiry date.

cards.title: Order tolerance and allocation of receipts back to purchase requests
cards.body:
Receiving more than the ordered quantity plus the allowed tolerance, by quantity or percentage, triggers a warning, or a hard stop where the company configures it.
When a purchase order was raised from purchase requests, the accepted quantity is distributed to those requests, and the request totals must equal the line's accepted quantity.
Each request line carrying quantity needs a warehouse, and reserved requests must have their reserved quantity fully covered.
Saving recalculates the status of the purchase order, gate pass, service order, request, sales order and stock transfer it references.

cards.title: Authorisation, stock posting and finance reconciliation on the GRN
cards.body:
A receipt moves from Initial to Release to Authorized; release and authorisation record the user and date, and with multi-level approval only the last-level approver can authorise.
Stock is increased only on authorisation, and only after these checks pass: rejected quantity per line cannot exceed the rejection recorded at inspection, weighment must exist where weighment controls the quantity, and the month must not be locked for stock.
Where the company forces inspection, inspection is always required before the material counts as accepted stock.
If rejected material is to be returned through a dispatch challan, the rejected quantity is included in the finance posting quantity.
On authorisation the accounting voucher must agree with the stock lot value within tolerance, and finance-enabled companies must have a voucher for valued lots.
For raw material received on challan quantity, the authorised rate can be recomputed so the vendor is paid on the challan quantity.
Together these controls make sure stock, inspection and the general ledger always tell the same story.

items.title: Inspection Intimation
items.context: Material Management › Goods Receipt and Quality Inspection › Inspection Intimation

cards.title: Why stores send an Inspection Intimation
cards.body:
An Inspection Intimation is a numbered letter telling the inspecting department which received items are waiting for quality inspection.
Storekeepers raise it after material arrives on a receipt note flagged as requiring inspection, before that receipt is authorised.
It formally triggers and tracks inspection, so no inspected receipt is accepted without a recorded request.

cards.title: Which receipt lines can be intimated and to whom
cards.body:
Only lines of receipt notes flagged for inspection, within the chosen date range and division, and not yet authorised are listed.
A receipt line, purchase request split or lot split already on another intimation is never offered again, so each line is intimated once.
At least one line must be selected and each needs an inspecting department, defaulting from the purchase request or the receipt.
Receipt dates cannot be after the intimation date, and release and authorisation stamp the user and date.

items.title: Inspection Entry
items.context: Material Management › Goods Receipt and Quality Inspection › Inspection Entry

cards.title: Purpose of the Inspection Entry
cards.body:
Inspection Entry records the result of quality inspection on received goods: accepted and rejected quantity, reasons, rejected serials and quality parameter values.
Quality controllers complete it after the inspection intimation is authorised and before the receipt note is authorised.
Only accepted material is taken into stock, and rejections are documented for vendor follow-up.

cards.title: Recording accepted and rejected quantities correctly
cards.body:
A department and an inspection officer are mandatory, and at least one intimated line must be selected.
Only lines on an authorised intimation, whose receipt note is not yet authorised and which are not on another inspection, are offered.
Accepted quantity cannot exceed received quantity, and rejected quantity is received minus accepted.
Any rejection requires a reason, and receipt and intimation dates cannot be after the inspection date.
Coil items require width and thickness.

cards.title: How an authorised inspection cascades into the receipt note and stock
cards.body:
When an inspection is authorised, each line writes the rejected quantity back to the receipt note, reducing its accepted quantity and the stock quantity after unit conversion.
Heat numbers on lots are updated, and purchase request reservations are reduced where the receipt line has a single reservation.
For serial-tracked items, the number of rejected serials must equal the rejected quantity, and the same serial cannot be rejected twice on one item line.
Where purchase-order quality matching is configured, each measured parameter must match the order's standard value or range, otherwise the inspection is blocked or warned.
Weighbridge-controlled companies cannot cover several receipt notes in one inspection for qualifying raw material lines.
Because the receipt note later refuses rejected quantities above the inspection result, the inspection becomes the governing quality decision for the consignment.

items.title: Gate Pass In
items.context: Material Management › Gate Operations › Gate Pass In

cards.title: What Gate Pass In records at the factory gate
cards.body:
Gate Pass In records material entering the premises that is not a normal purchase receipt.
Typical cases are contractor material, direct returnable or non-returnable receipts, material coming back against an earlier Gate Pass Out, loans, replacements and subcontract or repair material returning.
It closes off outstanding outward material and gives a dated record of who brought what in.

cards.title: Reference documents, balance limits and date pairing on inward passes
cards.body:
The pass type decides which references are offered: open outward passes of the same type, receipt notes with replaceable quantity, service orders, subcontract orders or service calls.
For returns against outward passes, loans and subcontract receipts, the received quantity cannot exceed the outstanding balance.
Challan, lorry receipt, weighment slip and e-way bill numbers must come with their dates, none later than the pass date.
A returnable date is mandatory for direct returnable receipts and loans taken, and cannot be before the pass date.

cards.title: Stock effects, loan valuation and outward pass closure on authorisation
cards.body:
Only authorised inward passes move stock, and the effect depends on the pass type.
Replacement receipts update the original receipt-note lot, loans received go into main stock at the line rate, repair returns go into repair stock, and subcontract receipts are spread across the order's requisitions first-in-first-out before entering main or reusable stock.
Contractor material, returnable receipts and service-related passes do not change stock at all.
A loan return must use the same rate as the original outward pass, and authorised loan passes post a journal voucher for the line value.
Every saved line recalculates the linked Gate Pass Out as completed or partly received, so outstanding returnable material is always visible.
Serial numbers are registered against the received lots once stock is posted.

items.title: Gate Pass Out
items.context: Material Management › Gate Operations › Gate Pass Out

cards.title: What Gate Pass Out controls when material leaves
cards.body:
Gate Pass Out records material physically leaving the premises other than through a sales invoice.
It covers returns to parties, loans given, subcontracting, repairs and service, and passes raised for delivery challans.
Stock is reduced at the right value, and material that must come back can be tracked against a later Gate Pass In.

cards.title: Despatch quantity, stock limits and returnable dates
cards.body:
Despatch quantity must be above zero and, for returns and replacements, cannot exceed the open balance of the reference.
For loans and stock-based types, the quantity cannot exceed the current stock and, where relevant, the stock available on the document date.
A returnable date is mandatory for direct returnable passes and loans given, and cannot be earlier than the pass date.
The pass date cannot be earlier than its reference document date, and freight basis is required unless a transport route is defined.

cards.title: Lot allocation, GST movement rules and the stock effect of outward passes
cards.body:
For loans, subcontract and repair passes, the despatch quantity is allocated to stock lots first-in-first-out, and the line rate becomes lot amount divided by quantity; lot totals must equal the line quantity and no lot can exceed its stock.
For subcontract orders, quantities are checked against the material already issued to that order.
While a pass is unauthorised its lots are reserved; on authorisation stock is issued, serial numbers are registered and the related inward pass status is recalculated.
Bill-to-ship-to style GST movements require a dispatch-from party and location, and the bill-from and dispatch-from GST numbers must differ where configured.
Authorised loan passes post a journal voucher, and the whole pass, including lines, notes, route and approvals, is saved as one unit and rolled back on any error.

items.title: Gate In for Outward Movement
items.context: Material Management › Gate Operations › Gate In for Outward Movement

cards.title: What Gate In for outward movement records
cards.body:
Gate In for outward movement records the arrival at the factory gate of a vehicle that will load goods for a customer.
Security records transporter, vehicle, driver, loading condition, in time and customer details, either directly or against a dispatch advice.
It gives an auditable arrival record and is the document that weighment and gate out build on.

cards.title: Blacklist, dispatch advice and same-day repeat controls
cards.body:
A blacklisted vehicle number, compared without spaces, cannot be gated in.
A gate in against a dispatch advice needs that advice, which must not already be used by another gate in or weighment; choosing it fills vehicle, transporter, driver and customer details.
A second gate in of the same vehicle on the same date is refused or warned unless the vehicle is on the multiple-entry list.
In time must be recorded where configured, and release or authorisation stamps the user and date.

items.title: Gate In for Outward Movement Amendment
items.context: Material Management › Gate Operations › Gate In for Outward Movement Amendment

cards.title: When a Gate In for outward movement is amended
cards.body:
The Gate In Amendment corrects the customer location, agent and item list of an authorised outward gate in.
It is used when customer or load details were recorded wrongly after authorisation but before weighment is final.
The gate in remains usable downstream with correct customer data, without raising a new document.

cards.title: Eligible gate ins and what can change
cards.body:
Only authorised gate ins of the company, authorised within the last month, with no weighment or a non-final weighment, can be amended.
Only customer location, agent and the item list are saved; every other detail is shown for reference only.
Once weighment is final, the gate in can no longer be corrected through this amendment.
This narrow scope keeps vehicle and arrival evidence intact while allowing commercial details to be fixed.

items.title: Vehicle Gate Out
items.context: Material Management › Gate Operations › Vehicle Gate Out

cards.title: Purpose of the Vehicle Gate Out
cards.body:
Vehicle Gate Out records the departure of a vehicle that entered the premises, with gate-out time, loading condition and the invoices it took out.
It covers outward customer vehicles and inward supplier vehicles recorded by gate entry.
It ties dispatched invoices to the carrying vehicle and shows which vehicles are still on site.

cards.title: Linking to the gate in, timing and invoice rules
cards.body:
A gate-in number is mandatory; only authorised gate ins of the company and division not already used on another gate out are offered.
Gate-out time must be recorded and cannot be earlier than the gate-in time, and the document date cannot precede the gate-in date.
Only authorised invoices not on another gate out are offered, and the same invoice cannot be listed twice; inward gate entries carry no invoices.
When no invoice is listed, a reason is mandatory, and weighment tare and gross weights are shown for reference.

items.title: Warehouse
items.context: Material Management › Inventory Storage and Issue › Warehouse

cards.title: What the Warehouse master defines
cards.body:
The Warehouse master defines the stores in which inventory is held, with ownership, address, company and division assignment and allowed items.
Stores managers create warehouses when a new store, third-party warehouse or division store opens.
Receipts, issues and transfers can only use valid warehouses for valid items.

cards.title: Ownership, item assignment and valuation setup
cards.body:
A warehouse is owned or party-held; a party name applies only to party-owned warehouses.
Items are assigned for every selected company and division, and selecting a group or sub group selects all its items.
Choosing a city fills state and country, and the full address is composed automatically.
Creating a warehouse prepares stock valuation settings for each company, and each new company or division assignment adds a valuation entry.

items.title: Bin Card
items.context: Material Management › Inventory Storage and Issue › Bin Card

cards.title: What a BIN Card records for the stores
cards.body:
A BIN Card is the register of storage bins inside each warehouse, together with the items allowed in each bin.
The stores manager maintains it when a store is laid out or reorganised.
It lets material be located and put away consistently, and receipts and returns of bin-managed items are posted into these bins.

cards.title: Mapping items to a bin by sub group or by individual item
cards.body:
Each bin belongs to a warehouse and may optionally be tied to a division linked to that warehouse; changing the warehouse clears the division.
Items are mapped to the bin either sub group wise, where choosing a sub group as default brings in all its items, or item wise, where individual items are chosen.
New bins start in sub group wise mode, and at least one item must be selected before the bin can be saved.
A maximum capacity can be recorded optionally to guide storage planning.

items.title: Material Issue
items.context: Material Management › Inventory Storage and Issue › Material Issue

cards.title: Purpose and ownership of the Material Issue
cards.body:
The Material Issue records material leaving a warehouse to an employee, contractor, shop floor or vendor against a business need.
Storekeepers issue material for consumption, capital work, subcontracting, repair, maintenance, service, production or as a returnable loan.
Stock is reduced lot by lot at the correct value and the cost is charged to the right department, cost center and account.

cards.title: Issue sources, issue types and who receives the material
cards.body:
An issue can be direct or made against a reference document such as a material request, subcontract order, maintenance order or customer service order.
The issue type, such as revenue, capital or repairable, decides how the cost is treated, and the issue-to choice decides whether the receiver is an employee, contractor or vendor.
New issues default to own stock, non-returnable and non-chargeable.

cards.title: Quantity, stock availability and reference balance checks
cards.body:
Ownership, source, warehouse, department and issue type are mandatory, and the department must belong to the issue's division.
Every selected line needs a quantity above zero, plus pieces for piece-managed items, and the same item and make cannot repeat.
Quantity cannot exceed current stock or stock on the issue date.
For reference-based issues, the total issued per item and make cannot exceed the reference document's open balance.
The issue date cannot precede the reference date, and where cost centers apply every line needs one.

cards.title: Lot selection, capital rules and ledger reconciliation on authorisation
cards.body:
Lots selected for a line must total the issued quantity, cannot exceed available stock after other lines, and cannot be received after the issue date.
Capital and non-capital lots cannot be mixed; capital lots can be used only for capital issues, and a non-capital item on a capital issue triggers a warning.
A repairable issue type is allowed only against a repairable customer service order, and internal warehouses can be used only for subcontract issues.
Capital issues must debit a work-in-progress account, while revenue and raw material issues must debit a consumption account.
An unauthorised issue holds its lots; on authorisation stock is reduced and the voucher must match lot values per item, otherwise the whole save is rolled back.
Authorised issues are final, and deletion is blocked once production has been booked against the issue or goods are received against its subcontract order.

items.title: Raw Material Issue
items.context: Material Management › Inventory Storage and Issue › Raw Material Issue

cards.title: What the Raw Material Issue is designed for
cards.body:
The Raw Material Issue issues stock from a warehouse to a department by stock item group rather than by individual item.
Stores teams use it when departments draw raw or intermediate material for production by grade or material group.
Stock is reduced from the oldest lots first, valued at lot rates and charged to the department and cost center.

cards.title: Group-wise quantities, oldest-first lots and stock limits
cards.body:
Only raw material and similar item types are offered, raw material by default, and at least one group line is required.
Entering a quantity allocates lots oldest received first; amount is lot quantity times lot rate and rate is amount divided by quantity.
Quantity cannot exceed current stock or stock on the issue date, and selected lots must equal the line quantity.
The issue date cannot be earlier than the latest receipt date of the selected lots, and departments must belong to the selected division.

cards.title: Authorisation, voucher matching and automatic fuel consumption
cards.body:
Every group-wise issue is saved as a direct, revenue, non-returnable, non-chargeable issue.
One item line is created per distinct item, make, grade and cost center among the selected lots.
While unauthorised, lot quantities are recorded as pending issues; on authorisation lot stock is reduced.
When finance applies, a voucher is built from the selected lots and, on an authorised save, its amounts must match the lot movement values or the save is rolled back.
Where enabled, authorising an issue of a fuel item to a cost center mapped to exactly one vehicle automatically creates a fuel consumption entry, linking stores issues to fleet maintenance records.

items.title: Material Return
items.context: Material Management › Inventory Storage and Issue › Material Return

cards.title: Why stores record a Material Return
cards.body:
A Material Return brings unused, excess or scrap material back into a warehouse and reverses its consumption.
It is used when material issued earlier, or held by a person or job, is handed back to stores.
Stock and consumption cost are corrected, at the original issue value when the return is against an issue.

cards.title: Which issues can be returned and how much
cards.body:
Only authorised issues of the same company, warehouse, department and division with a positive balance, issued within the configured return period, are offered.
Selected issues must share issue type and chargeable status, and capital and non-capital items cannot be returned together.
Returned quantity cannot be zero and cannot exceed the issue balance.
Direct returns need a rate above zero unless returned at zero value, and the return date cannot precede the issue date.

cards.title: Lot-level valuation and stock receipt for returns
cards.body:
Returns against issues spread the returned quantity over the original issue lots in order, up to each lot's balance, and take rate and amount from those lots, so stock comes back at its original cost.
A return cannot exceed what was issued less production or fuel already consumed against it, a scrap return needs a scrap setting, and items used in a cost allocation cannot be returned.
Bin-managed items need bin quantities that total the returned quantity, and expiry-tracked items need a valid expiry date.
On authorisation, stock is received: scrap returns as the scrap item, issue returns into new lots linked to the original lots with their batch and rate, and direct returns as new lots, with serial numbers re-added.
Return sources available depend on stock nature, for example repair stock can also be returned against tyre repair requests.

items.title: Stock Transfer
items.context: Material Management › Stock Transfer › Stock Transfer

cards.title: What a Stock Transfer does
cards.body:
A Stock Transfer issues stock from specific lots of one warehouse and receives it into another.
It covers moves between warehouses, divisions or group companies, and conversions of stock nature such as capital to revenue.
Lot-wise stock, its valuation and inter-company finance entries stay consistent at both ends.

cards.title: Transfer types, sources and one-step versus two-step processing
cards.body:
A transfer can be by company, division, warehouse or material, and each type allows certain sources: direct, purchase order freight route or work order.
One-step transfers issue and receive in the same document, while two-step transfers only issue here and the receiving unit records a receipt note later.
Material conversions are always one-step.

cards.title: Issue quantity, lot allocation and receipt line rules
cards.body:
Issue quantity must be non-zero and cannot exceed current stock or stock on the document date.
Lots are allocated automatically or picked manually; lot totals must equal the line quantity, and lots tied to a freight route are blocked except for purchase order transfers.
For purchase order transfers, the total moved cannot exceed the order quantity plus tolerance.
In one-step transfers receipt lines are rebuilt from issue lines, total receipt value must equal total issue value, and the destination division must differ from the source division.

cards.title: Capital items, finance vouchers and lot reconciliation on transfers
cards.body:
When finance and the asset module apply, capital items on non-order transfers need asset tags equal to each lot quantity, all lines must then be capital, and processing must be two-step.
Capital-to-revenue conversions offer only unreserved capital lots and receive the stock as non-capital.
Company and division transfers to a different finance book post an inter-book issue voucher, and moving capital items there also requires an asset disposal posting.
Unauthorised transfers hold their lots as pending issues; on authorisation lots are issued with their cost center, bin and reservation, and one-step receipts create new lots carrying capital, heat, serial and order references.
On an authorised save, the issue and receiving vouchers must agree with lot values within tolerance, and value differences above a small limit are refused.
Where lot-to-lot transfer is used, mixed multi-item direct transfers cannot include heat-numbered or quality-graded lots.

items.title: Inter Unit Stock Transfer
items.context: Material Management › Stock Transfer › Inter Unit Stock Transfer

cards.title: What an Inter Unit Stock Transfer is for
cards.body:
An Inter Unit Stock Transfer moves stock from a warehouse of the current company to a warehouse of another group company in a single step.
It is used when material moves between group units without a separate goods receipt at the destination.
One document updates the stock and the inter-company finance entries of both units.

cards.title: Issue lots, receipt lines and the value balance
cards.body:
The from warehouse belongs to the current company and division, and the to warehouse is an authorised warehouse of the destination company; both are mandatory.
Issue quantity cannot exceed current stock or stock on the document date, and lots are allocated automatically, with the line rate equal to lot value divided by quantity.
Receipt lines are built from the issue lines using the destination company's mapped item, and each receipt item must be mapped to the destination warehouse.
Total receipt value must equal total issue value.

cards.title: Inter-company vouchers, asset disposal and authorisation of unit transfers
cards.body:
Every inter-unit transfer is a direct, one-step company transfer, so the issue and the receipt are posted by the same document.
An issue journal is created using the destination company's finance book and a receiving journal in the destination company's posting setup; a missing book stops the transfer.
When capital items move to a company with a different finance book, an asset disposal posting with asset deductions is required and saved on authorisation.
While unauthorised, the selected lots are recorded as pending issues so they cannot be consumed twice.
On authorisation, lots are issued from the source warehouse and new lots received at receipt rates into the destination; a value difference above a small rounding limit is refused.
The full document is saved as one transaction and rolled back on any error.

items.title: Quantity and Value Adjustment in Stock Transfer
items.context: Material Management › Stock Transfer › Quantity and Value Adjustment in Stock Transfer

cards.title: What a quantity and value adjustment in stock transfer corrects
cards.body:
A Quantity and Value Adjustment compares what left a source with what actually arrived at the end of a stock movement chain.
It is prepared after a purchase order with a multi-leg freight route is manually closed, or after a direct warehouse transfer is received.
The value difference is spread over the received lots so stock value and moving average rates reflect true cost.

cards.title: Eligible references and leg-by-leg quantity balancing
cards.body:
For purchase orders, only the latest authorised amendment of a manually closed order with a multi-leg route, not used by another adjustment, can be chosen.
For stock transfers, only authorised direct warehouse transfers without route lines can be chosen.
Lines are calculated per item, make, grade and leg, showing receipt, onward transfer, consumption, return and shortage or excess.
On intermediate legs, received less transferred less consumed must be zero, and lines are read-only.

cards.title: Lot revaluation, price variance and in-transit loss postings
cards.body:
On authorisation, received normal-stock lots with a difference are collected; any such lot dated after the adjustment stops the save.
Each lot receives a bill adjustment and its moving average rate is recalculated.
The journal posts stock and price variance depending on whether the new rate stays within the allowed band, clears stock in transit, and books lost-in-transit when goods were sent but never received.
Small rounding differences are absorbed, and the voucher must reconcile with this document's lot adjustments.
For purchase order references, the route's stock transfers, all amendments and the order itself are closed once the adjustment is saved.
This is how freight-route losses and gains finally reach inventory value and the ledger.

items.title: Single Item Opening
items.context: Material Management › Stock Adjustment and Opening › Single Item Opening

cards.title: When Single Item Opening is used
cards.body:
Single Item Opening records the opening stock of one item at a time for a chosen division, warehouse, ownership, stock nature and capital or non-capital stock type.
It is used when a company starts using inventory or an item's opening position must be corrected before the books are closed.
Lot details such as make, batch, bill, expiry and serial numbers are captured so stock can be tracked later.

cards.title: Opening lines, quantities and values must reconcile
cards.body:
Only active goods items mapped to the chosen warehouse and division and matching the stock type are offered.
Each detail line needs a bill number, bill date and quantity above zero, and the opening quantity must equal the total of the lines.
Line amount is quantity times rate; without detail lines, one lot is saved at opening amount divided by opening quantity.
Expiry-managed items need expiry dates, never earlier than the opening date, and where finance applies the item must have a stock account and a stock clearing account.

items.title: Multi Item Opening
items.context: Material Management › Stock Adjustment and Opening › Multi Item Opening

cards.title: Purpose of Multi Item Opening
cards.body:
Multi Item Opening loads the opening stock of many items in one session at the inventory start date.
It is used when a company starts using inventory or a new warehouse is brought into the system.
Stock ledgers and lot-wise stock then start from a known quantity and value that finance opening balances can match.

cards.title: Eligible items, lot splits and rates for opening stock
cards.body:
Only active, authorised goods items mapped to the warehouse and division and matching the stock type are offered; an item that already has an opening lot for that combination is not offered again.
Every selected item needs a non-zero quantity and, if not split into lots, a rate; total amount is quantity times rate.
Lot splits must add up to the item quantity, each lot needs a department, cost center, bin or batch and a rate, and duplicate lot combinations are refused.
Expiry-managed items need an expiry date not before the opening date.

cards.title: Finance opening balances, issued lots and balance sheet protection
cards.body:
When finance applies and non-capital stock is loaded, each item must have a stock account and a stock clearing account.
Finance opening balances are updated only for own stock of normal nature, only for non-capital lots, and only when the finance module is active.
For cost-center-applicable items, lot amounts carrying a cost center must add up to the item's total value.
Once a lot has been issued, only its quantity can change, and never below the issued quantity; existing lots cannot be removed.
Lots marked as reserved create a reservation for their quantity, tied to the cost center where given.
After the company has prepared a balance sheet, opening lots can no longer be saved, protecting closed financial figures.

items.title: Physical Stock Verification
items.context: Material Management › Stock Adjustment and Opening › Physical Stock Verification

cards.title: Purpose of Physical Stock Verification
cards.body:
Physical Stock Verification records a count of physical stock in one warehouse and compares counted quantities with book quantities.
It is prepared when a warehouse is physically counted and the count must be formally authorised before any correction is booked.
The result is an auditable count with the difference per item and bin.

cards.title: Counting rules and how book quantity is derived
cards.body:
Only stock-managed goods items mapped to the company, warehouse and division can be counted, and at least one item is required.
Book quantity is opening stock before the count date plus receipts less issues, for the same warehouse, division, ownership, item, make and attribute, excluding capital stock.
For bin-managed items, the counted bin quantities must total the actual quantity.
The verification date cannot precede the document date and is mandatory for every item before authorisation.

cards.title: Why a verification never changes stock and how adjustments follow
cards.body:
Saving or authorising a verification changes no stock lot, bin or accounting voucher; it is purely an authorised record of the count.
A later Stock Adjustment offers only items from authorised verifications whose counted quantity differs from the book quantity and that have not already been adjusted.
An authorised verification reopens with its stored quantities, while an unauthorised one recalculates opening, receipts, issues and bin figures from current stock.
Release and authorisation stamp the user and time, giving auditors evidence of who counted and who approved.
Separating the count from the correction enforces segregation of duties between counting staff and those who change stock values.

items.title: Stock Adjustment
items.context: Material Management › Stock Adjustment and Opening › Stock Adjustment

cards.title: Why a Stock Adjustment follows a stock count
cards.body:
A Stock Adjustment corrects book stock to match what was physically counted.
It converts differences from an authorised physical stock verification into stock receipts for excess and stock issues for shortage, with their value.
Book stock, lot balances and stock value then agree with the count, and the difference is posted to finance.

cards.title: Verification reference and adjustment line rules
cards.body:
When the source is a stock verification, the reference is mandatory and the adjustment date cannot precede the verification date.
Only authorised verifications of the same warehouse and division with unadjusted differences are offered.
Adjusted quantity is the counted quantity less system quantity, valued at the latest received lot rate.
At least one line must be selected, with no repeated item, make and attribute and no zero adjustment; capital and non-capital items cannot be mixed.

cards.title: Lot-level posting of excess and shortage and ledger reconciliation
cards.body:
Shortages are allocated across available lots, or bin by bin for bin-managed items, and valued at minus quantity times lot rate.
Excess is received as new lots; for measured items stock quantity is derived from unit weight, length, width and pieces.
At save, lot totals must equal the absolute adjusted quantity, bin issues must match bin differences, and shortages cannot exceed current or on-date stock.
While unauthorised, shortage lots are held as pending issues; on authorisation stock is received or issued and serial numbers registered.
When finance applies, a journal for the adjusted amount is created, and the voucher must agree with lot values or the entire save is rolled back.
Where production posting rules apply, intermediate and finished goods are adjusted at zero value.

items.title: Value Stock Adjustment
items.context: Material Management › Stock Adjustment and Opening › Value Stock Adjustment

cards.title: What a Value Stock Adjustment corrects
cards.body:
A Value Stock Adjustment changes the book value of selected stock lots in a warehouse without changing their quantity.
It is used when stock is found to be over- or under-valued, for example after a price correction.
Lot rates and stock value then reflect the corrected value, and the difference can be posted to finance.

cards.title: Selecting lots and entering the corrected value
cards.body:
Only active items assigned to the warehouse and division are offered; choosing an item brings in all lots with positive stock on the document date.
Each line needs an actual amount and a non-zero on-date stock, with at least one selected lot and no selected lot at zero stock.
The adjusted amount is actual amount less stock amount; an item-level actual amount is spread across the selected lots in proportion to their value.
A selected lot cannot keep its actual amount equal to its stock amount, and capital and non-capital items cannot be mixed.

cards.title: Lot revaluation on authorisation and voucher-to-lot reconciliation
cards.body:
On authorisation, each selected lot that has a receipt and billing record receives a rate difference equal to actual amount minus stock amount, divided by the lot's balance quantity at that moment.
Because the difference is spread over the remaining balance, later issues from the lot automatically carry the corrected rate.
If a lot's stock value has changed since it was fetched, the user is warned before continuing.
When finance applies, a journal for the total adjusted amount is created on the document date, and for authorised documents the voucher must agree with lot values or the save is rolled back.
Changing the document date refreshes stock figures and rebuilds the voucher, but not lot amounts, so values should be reviewed after date changes.

items.title: Change Material Stock Nature
items.context: Material Management › Stock Adjustment and Opening › Change Material Stock Nature

cards.title: What Change Material Stock Nature requests
cards.body:
Change Material Stock Nature records a formal request to reclassify the stock nature of selected stock lots in a warehouse.
It is used when stock currently held as capital stock must be treated differently.
The change is raised against exact lots with a requester, a reason and an approval status instead of being agreed informally.

cards.title: Eligible warehouses, items and lots and how approval is stamped
cards.body:
Warehouses follow the selected division, and items are limited to stock-managed items mapped to that warehouse that currently hold capital lots.
Only capital lots with stock on the document date are offered, and a lot is always selected whole.
The item quantity is the total of the selected lot quantities, and at least one item line is required.
Releasing the document stamps the releaser and time, and authorising stamps the authoriser and time.

items.title: Change Stock Allocation
items.context: Material Management › Stock Adjustment and Opening › Change Stock Allocation

cards.title: Why stores use Change Stock Allocation
cards.body:
Change Stock Allocation re-allocates the reserved split of an item's stock lots in a warehouse.
It is used when stock reserved for one purpose, such as a sales order, must be released or reserved for another, such as a job card or cost center.
Reservations stay accurate and traceable to a requester, a reason and an approval.

cards.title: Allocation lines must account for the whole lot balance
cards.body:
Only owned, non-capital, non-rejected lots with a balance, received on or before the document date, are offered.
Each lot is split into lines of Unreserved, Cost Center, Job Card or Sales Order; every reserved line needs a reference document and a non-zero quantity, and the same purpose and document cannot repeat.
The total of a lot's lines must equal its balance quantity; a shortfall is never allowed.
For specific stock-managed item types, an excess of up to three percent is accepted after a warning.

cards.title: Pending holds and what authorisation does to reservations
cards.body:
While a reallocation document is unauthorised, the lots it covers are held so other users see a reduced available balance; holds are rebuilt on every save and removed on delete.
On authorisation, each selected lot is marked reserved, its existing reservation balances are closed out, and one new reservation is created for each saved line against the cost center, job card or sales order.
Unreserved lines are added back as free stock.
After applying the change, the lot balance and the total of its reservation balances must agree within a small tolerance, otherwise the save is rejected.
Releaser and authoriser are stamped with time, giving a full audit trail of why reserved stock changed hands.

items.title: Budget
items.context: Material Management › Indent and Budget › Budget

cards.title: Why the company records a Budget before buying
cards.body:
A Budget records approved spending limits for a validity period, split by divisions and departments, item sub groups and items, or cost centers.
It is set when a financial year or period starts and management fixes what each area may spend.
Purchase requests and purchase orders are then checked against this recorded limit rather than an informal intention.

cards.title: Budget types, validity and the amounts kept per line
cards.body:
The budget type is chosen when the budget is created and cannot be changed afterwards.
The entry date must lie within the current financial year, the validity end must be later than the validity start, and no two budgets of the company may overlap in validity, whatever their type.
Each selected line holds a budget amount and a utilised amount, and the balance is budget minus utilised.
Utilised amount may never exceed the budget amount, and for items the utilised quantity may not exceed the budgeted quantity.

cards.title: Hierarchical budget limits, version zero and authorization effects
cards.body:
Budgets are hierarchical: selecting a parent selects its children and selecting a child selects its parent, across divisions and departments or the cost center tree.
The departments under a division may not together exceed the division's budget or utilisation, and child cost centers may not exceed their parent.
Header totals are the sums of the selected divisions, sub groups or top-level cost centers.
The first save creates the budget together with its version zero; while the budget is still on version zero, every save updates both the version and the live budget.
Marking the budget as authorised records the authoriser and date and makes the budget the authorised limit; otherwise it is held as not authorised.
Later changes must go through Budget Amendment so that each revision remains traceable.

items.title: Budget Amendment
items.context: Material Management › Indent and Budget › Budget Amendment

cards.title: What a Budget Amendment is used for
cards.body:
A Budget Amendment revises an approved budget without overwriting its history.
It is used when a spending limit, validity period or selected lines must change after the budget was created or authorised.
Each change becomes a new numbered version, so finance can always see how the limit evolved.

cards.title: Which budgets can be amended and what stays fixed
cards.body:
Only budgets whose newest version is authorised can be amended, so a budget with a pending unauthorised amendment must wait until that one is authorised or deleted.
The budget code, original entry date and budget type cannot be changed in an amendment.
The amendment date must fall within the current financial year and respect the back-date and future-date limits set for the screen.
Validity end must be later than validity start, and the same selection and amount rules as the original budget apply.

cards.title: How authorising an amendment replaces the live budget
cards.body:
An unauthorised amendment is stored only in the amendment records, so the budget in force keeps controlling purchases unchanged.
When the amendment is authorised, either on first save or on a later update, the live budget's header takes the amended values and its lines are replaced by the amendment lines.
The authoriser and date are recorded when authorisation is given.
Utilised amounts may not exceed budget amounts, departments must stay within their division and child cost centers within their parent, exactly as on the original budget.
These amount checks are enforced at entry, so reviewers should confirm totals carefully before authorising.
This design keeps a full version history while guaranteeing only approved figures ever govern requisitions and orders.

items.title: Indent Default Setting
items.context: Material Management › Indent and Budget › Indent Default Setting

cards.title: Why procurement units need an Indent Default Setting
cards.body:
Indent Default Setting stores, per procurement unit, the default values used when purchase requests and release orders are generated automatically.
It is maintained when a unit is introduced to automatic indenting or its defaults change.
Auto-generated requests then carry complete and consistent header values without anyone typing them.

cards.title: Eligible units, defaults held and the one-setting rule
cards.body:
Only active procurement units of the logged-in company that have an execution unit can be configured.
The setting holds maximum items per request, warehouse, cost center, department, requested by, prepared by, number series for requests and release orders, and the status new requests start in.
Departments are limited to the unit's division, and several defaults may be left empty.
A unit can never have two settings: saving updates the existing one or creates it if none exists.

items.title: Procurement Unit
items.context: Material Management › Material Planning and Replenishment › Procurement Unit

cards.title: What a Procurement Unit groups together
cards.body:
A Procurement Unit is a group of companies, or divisions where they apply, that plan and buy material together.
It is set up when the group decides which companies should pool demand, or when that grouping changes.
Planning and buying are pooled per unit, with one company or division executing the purchases.

cards.title: Exclusive membership, one execution unit and planning jobs
cards.body:
The unit name is mandatory and unique, and a new unit receives an automatic code.
A company or division can belong to only one procurement unit, so members already used elsewhere are not offered.
Exactly one member must be marked as the execution unit that places orders.
Saving registers the unit for the automatic indent and consumption history jobs, and the tracked item types define which materials the unit plans.

items.title: Material Planning Type Assignment
items.context: Material Management › Material Planning and Replenishment › Material Planning Type Assignment

cards.title: Purpose of assigning material planning types
cards.body:
Material planning type assignment decides, for each material planning unit, which planning type applies to each critical item.
Planners set it when a planning unit is created or when an item moves to a different planning approach.
Each critical item is planned in one declared way, and later settings ask only for the figures relevant to that way.

cards.title: Items in scope and how planning types are saved
cards.body:
Only active planning units of the logged-in company are offered.
Items listed are critical items active in the company and stocked in at least one warehouse of the unit.
At least one item must carry a planning type, and only items with a type are saved; a planning type can be applied to all listed items at once.
The assignment is effective from the company's inventory start date, and saving again for the same unit replaces its items.

items.title: Material Planning Setting
items.context: Material Management › Material Planning and Replenishment › Material Planning Setting

cards.title: What a Material Planning Setting records
cards.body:
A Material Planning Setting records dated stock control quantities for each critical item of a planning unit: minimum, maximum, reorder level and reorder quantity.
Planners create it when levels are first set and whenever they are revised from a given date.
Stock reports compare stock with the latest agreed levels while earlier levels stay on record.

cards.title: Min-max and reorder rules by planning type
cards.body:
Items come from the unit's planning type assignment, and at least one item needs a minimum quantity or reorder level.
Min-max items must have both minimum and maximum, with minimum less than maximum.
Reorder items must have both reorder level and reorder quantity.
Fields not relevant to an item's planning type cannot be edited.
A new setting cannot be saved if the same unit already has one with the same or later effective date, and unchanged lines are not stored again.

items.title: Material Consumption Pattern
items.context: Material Management › Material Planning and Replenishment › Material Consumption Pattern

cards.title: What a Material Consumption Pattern establishes
cards.body:
A Material Consumption Pattern fixes, item by item, the planning approach, consumption pattern and daily consumption rate for one planning unit and analysis period.
Planners prepare it before planning procurement, once enough consumption history exists.
Purchasing and stock planning then work from an agreed, reviewed consumption figure instead of estimates.

cards.title: Analysis periods, planning approaches and suggested patterns
cards.body:
The analysis can be date-wise, with the end date moved to month end, or by selected financial years.
Every selected item needs a planning approach, and past-consumption-based planning also needs a selected pattern and rate.
For date-wise analysis the system suggests weekly, fortnightly, monthly or quarterly patterns using a seventy percent rule on periods with consumption, and the rate is consumed quantity per day.
Planners can copy previous or suggested values into selected items, and only selected items are saved.

items.title: Change Consumption Pattern
items.context: Material Management › Material Planning and Replenishment › Change Consumption Pattern

cards.title: When planners use Change Consumption Pattern
cards.body:
Change Consumption Pattern lets a planner revise the planning figures of items already approved in the latest consumption pattern of a planning unit.
It is used when a supplier source, consumption rate or lead time changes for specific items.
Reorder figures are corrected quickly without re-running the full period analysis.

cards.title: Reorder point and maximum stock formulas
cards.body:
Only items from the latest authorised pattern of the unit are listed.
Reorder point equals safety days plus lead days, multiplied by the consumption rate.
Maximum stock equals reorder quantity plus reorder point, minus consumption rate times lead days.
Changing the source type replaces lead and safety days with the company's standard for that source.
Each selected item must have pattern, rate, source, safety days, lead days, reorder point, reorder quantity, maximum stock and safety stock, and all changes save together.

items.title: Material Lead and Safety Days Setting
items.context: Material Management › Material Planning and Replenishment › Material Lead and Safety Days Setting

cards.title: Purpose of the Material Lead and Safety Days Setting
cards.body:
The Material Lead and Safety Days Setting holds the standard lead days and safety days for each supply source.
Planners maintain it when planning is first set up or when supplier performance changes.
Planning documents then default these days by source instead of requiring them for every item.

cards.title: Every supply source needs complete standards
cards.body:
Each supply source line must have both a standard lead days value and a standard safety days value; the first missing value stops the save.
All lines are saved together in one confirmed transaction.
When a planner chooses a source on a consumption pattern or supplies source document, these standards overwrite the item's lead and safety days.
Reorder point and safety stock are therefore driven by these standards, so revising them changes future reorder levels.

items.title: Material Supplies Source
items.context: Material Management › Material Planning and Replenishment › Material Supplies Source

cards.title: What Material Supplies Source completes in planning
cards.body:
Material Supplies Source completes an authorised consumption pattern by deciding where each planned item is sourced from and how much stock to hold.
Planners use it after the pattern is authorised and before procurement is planned from it.
Reorder figures then reflect how and where each item is really bought.

cards.title: Source suggestions, standard days and stock level formulas
cards.body:
Only items planned on past consumption or fixed inventory level are shown, and at least one must be selected.
The suggested source is open supply when most past orders went to non-local cities, otherwise local supply.
Choosing a source replaces lead and safety days with the company standard for that source.
Reorder point is safety plus lead days times consumption rate, maximum stock is reorder quantity plus reorder point minus rate times lead days, and safety stock is rate times safety days.

items.title: Unit Rounding Setting
items.context: Material Management › Material Planning and Replenishment › Unit Rounding Setting

cards.title: Purpose of the Unit Rounding Setting
cards.body:
The Unit Rounding Setting decides, for each procurement unit, how planned quantities are rounded for each unit of measure.
It is set when a unit is introduced to automatic indenting or when the rounding policy changes.
Automatic purchase request quantities then follow a whole-unit policy instead of leaving fractions, for example for items counted in pieces.

cards.title: Rounding choices and their scope
cards.body:
Only two rules can be chosen for a unit of measure: no rounding, or ceiling to the next whole number.
Units of measure without an explicit setting default to no rounding.
Settings are kept separately for each procurement unit, and only active procurement units that include the company are offered.
The rule affects quantities generated by the automatic indent job, so a ceiling rule can slightly increase ordered quantities.

items.title: Go-Ahead Live
items.context: Material Management › Material Planning and Replenishment › Go-Ahead Live

cards.title: What Go-Ahead Live does for material planning
cards.body:
Go-Ahead Live is the formal release that puts authorised consumption patterns live for a procurement unit from a go-live date.
Planners use it after patterns are authorised and they want reorder point, reorder quantity, safety stock, maximum stock and lead days to start driving purchasing.
Planning values become effective only through this deliberate, reviewable release.

cards.title: How existing, new and overlapping items are presented before going live
cards.body:
A procurement unit is mandatory, and only authorised patterns of that unit not already used in another release are offered; at least one must be selected.
Existing items are those already live from an earlier release, new items come from the selected patterns, and items in both are shown as overlap with the new values.
The go-live date cannot be earlier than the document date.
Each item carries an auto-indent choice, which defaults to yes so planned items can trigger automatic purchase requests.

cards.title: Assessing inventory impact before a planning release is authorised
cards.body:
Before releasing, the planner can compute the inventory impact of the selected items.
Projected inventory is the weighted consumption rate multiplied by maximum stock, by safety stock and by the average of the two, and is compared with the current value of owned, accepted stock at the period start and each month end.
Results are summarised by material group and sub group so the financial effect of new planning norms is visible, but this projection is not stored.
Saving links the selected patterns to the release and stores the chosen items with their auto-indent flags; a re-save clears earlier items and links first.
Release and authorisation stamp the user and date, making the go-live decision auditable.

items.title: Job Control Sheet
items.context: Material Management › Material Planning and Replenishment › Job Control Sheet

cards.title: What the Job Control Sheet schedules
cards.body:
The Job Control Sheet schedules and controls two automatic jobs for each procurement unit: Auto Indent, which raises purchase requests for items below planned levels, and Consumption History, which collects weekly consumption.
Planners use it to run procurement planning unattended, or to pause and re-run a job.
Requests and history are produced on time without manual effort.

cards.title: Job schedules, running status and manual runs
cards.body:
Only active procurement units of the current company are offered.
Jobs can run hourly, daily, weekly on a chosen weekday, monthly, or on the first or last day of the month; a consumption history job needs a number of days above zero.
Setting a job to stopped disables it and setting it to running enables it, and saving recreates each scheduled job.
A manual run executes Auto Indent once per date in the chosen range regardless of status, and saving fails unless the job scheduler service is running.

items.title: Release Order Generation
items.context: Material Management › Material Planning and Replenishment › Release Order Generation

cards.title: What Release RO does with automatic purchase requests
cards.body:
Release RO turns automatically generated purchase requests into release orders against existing rate contracts.
It is used after the automatic indent process has raised requests and a rate contract exists for the items.
Routine replenishment is ordered quickly at agreed rates without keying orders by hand.

cards.title: Eligible request lines and matching the rate contract
cards.body:
Only authorised auto-procurement requests, not yet linked to any order and belonging to a planning unit that includes the company, are listed.
The contract used is the latest authorised rate contract containing the item and valid on the release date.
Selected lines are grouped by contract, one release order per contract, with the same item merged across requests and a quantity-weighted rate.
Supplier, terms, taxes and payment details are copied from the contract; the order starts in Initial status with one-year validity.

items.title: Item Supplemental Information
items.context: Material Management › Material Planning and Replenishment › Item Supplemental Information

cards.title: Purpose of Item Supplemental Information
cards.body:
Item Supplemental Information records extra descriptive values, such as identifying marks, against a specific received lot of an item.
It is completed after material is received on a receipt note or billed on a purchase bill and unit-level details must be captured.
Each lot or serial number can then carry its own details rather than only the item-level defaults.

cards.title: Which documents, serials and fields can be completed
cards.body:
Only items active for the current company are offered.
Documents offered are receipt-note or purchase-bill lots of the chosen item that are not yet fully covered by supplemental values.
Serial numbers offered are those of the document not yet issued and without values.
The fields shown are the supplementary fields assigned to the item and active in the company, together with the item master value for comparison, and blank lines are ignored.

items.title: Service Request
items.context: Material Management › Service and Subcontract Procurement › Service Request

cards.title: Purpose of a Service Request
cards.body:
A Service Request is an internal requisition for outside services or job work, together with the materials to be sent, returned or received back.
Departments raise it when processing, repair or activity-based work must be done by a subcontractor.
Service purchasing receives a controlled, approved demand with quantities, schedules and materials defined up front.

cards.title: Subcontract types, service lines and material lines
cards.body:
The subcontract type, such as service, conversion or activity, decides whether service lines or activity lines are entered, and the nature list follows the type.
Service lines need a quantity and unique service items, and activity lines need a valid activity, unit and non-zero quantity.
Material lines need activity or service, item, item flow and quantity; a returnable input needs a matching issuable input, and capital and non-capital items cannot mix.
A warehouse is required whenever material lines exist, and delivery schedules are validated against the request date.

cards.title: Item flow combinations and work-order based requests
cards.body:
Item flows are strictly combined: repairable items are allowed only on service requests, repair-nature requests need at least one repairable item, and conversion and activity requests need an issuable input and exactly one primary output per service or activity.
For activity work the first sequence needs an issuable input and the last a primary output.
Requests based on work orders list only authorised work orders with subcontract balance, and a work order's quantity cannot exceed its balance.
For mark-based products, requested quantity is allocated across work orders up to each balance.
Requests from material planning cannot exceed the planned quantity across all such requests.
References must be authorised and not fully requested, and the request moves through Initial, Release and Authorized with stamps.

items.title: Service RFQ
items.context: Material Management › Service and Subcontract Procurement › Service RFQ

cards.title: What a Service RFQ asks subcontractors for
cards.body:
A Service RFQ invites selected subcontractors and service vendors to quote for services, conversion jobs or activities.
Buyers raise it from an approved service request or a directly entered need, before placing a service order.
Every invited vendor receives the same requirement and deadlines, and linked request lines are tracked.

cards.title: Date sequence, service lines and vendor rules
cards.body:
Submission cannot precede the request date, opening cannot precede submission, and validity cannot precede opening.
Service and conversion requests need at least one item with quantity and a delivery date not before the request date; conversion items need an issuable input and a primary output.
Activity requests need valid activities with unit and quantity, plus input and output items.
At least one active service vendor with a location is required, and the same vendor cannot be invited twice.

cards.title: Linking service requests and controlling job work through gate passes
cards.body:
When raised against service requests, at least one authorised, open request must be selected; requests of different nature or product type cannot be combined, and none may be dated after the RFQ.
Quantities for a work order cannot exceed the work order quantity less what is already requested on other RFQs.
Where the company controls service work through gate passes, a job-work repair request allows only one vendor and one request, the request must already have an outward gate pass, and the invited vendor must be the gate pass vendor.
Each linked request line has its status recalculated from ordered quantities, including when lines are released by deletion.
These controls ensure material sent out for repair is quoted only by the party holding it.

items.title: Service Quotation
items.context: Material Management › Service and Subcontract Procurement › Service Quotation

cards.title: Purpose of a Service Quotation
cards.body:
A Service Quotation records a subcontractor's priced offer, with rates, taxes, delivery days and terms, against an authorised Service Request for Quotation.
It is entered when an invited service vendor submits its offer.
Offers arrive in one structured format per request and vendor, ready for comparison, agreements and orders.

cards.title: Eligible requests, vendor dates and service line checks
cards.body:
Only authorised service requests for quotation with an invited vendor who has not yet quoted are offered, and the vendor and location must be among those invited.
The vendor's quotation number is mandatory, its date cannot be after the entry date or before the request date, and validity cannot precede the entry date.
At least one line must be selected, each with quantity, rate, net amount above zero and non-zero delivery days.
Freight type and payment mode are mandatory, and additional cost lines need quantity and rate with an allowed tolerance.

items.title: Revised Service Quotation
items.context: Material Management › Service and Subcontract Procurement › Revised Service Quotation

cards.title: What a Revised Service Quotation keeps on record
cards.body:
A Revised Service Quotation is a numbered revision of a service vendor's quotation, kept beside the original.
It is used when the vendor changes price, terms or quantities after the service quotation was authorised.
Service agreements and orders then use the latest authorised offer while earlier offers remain traceable.

cards.title: Which service quotations can be revised and line checks
cards.body:
Only authorised service quotations at their latest revision, with no unauthorised revision pending, can be revised; the revision number is the latest plus one.
The vendor quotation date cannot be after the entry date or before the request date, and validity cannot precede the entry date.
Each line needs quantity, rate, a net amount above zero and non-zero delivery days.
Mandatory vendor, location, freight and payment details follow the same rules as the original service quotation, and an authorised revision becomes read-only.

items.title: Service Agreement
items.context: Material Management › Service and Subcontract Procurement › Service Agreement

cards.title: Purpose of a Service Agreement
cards.body:
A Service Agreement records a standing agreement with a service or subcontract vendor: agreed rates, quantities or amounts for services, conversion items or activities over a period.
It is used when terms have been agreed with a subcontractor, either from a winning quotation or negotiated directly.
Agreed prices and terms are stored once and reused by later service documents.

cards.title: Agreement types, line values and mandatory commercial terms
cards.body:
The subcontract type can be service, conversion or activity, and the agreement is by rate, quantity or amount, which decides what each line must carry.
Rate agreements need a rate, quantity agreements need quantity and rate, and amount agreements need an amount; agreement value is the sum of selected lines.
The period cannot start before the agreement date and must end after it starts.
Freight type, pay-to and bill-to parties and payment mode are mandatory, and tolerance applies only to quantity agreements.

cards.title: Agreements raised from quotations and their downstream use
cards.body:
An agreement can be direct or based on a quotation; a quotation source requires the reference, and its date cannot be after the agreement date.
Only authorised service quotations at their latest revision and still open are offered, and the vendor is limited to the quotation's vendor.
Lines from the quotation carry quantity and rate, and item, description and unit cannot be changed.
Each code can appear only once, and only selected lines are saved.
Once authorised, the agreement becomes a valid commercial basis for service orders and can be secured by a bank guarantee.
Release and authorisation stamp user and time.

items.title: Service Order
items.context: Material Management › Service and Subcontract Procurement › Service Order

cards.title: What a Service Order commits to a subcontractor
cards.body:
A Service Order places subcontract or service work on a vendor for services, conversion jobs or activities.
It is raised against a service quotation, service request, letter of intent or agreement, or placed directly, and holds input and output material, rates, schedules, taxes and terms.
It is the binding, approved order that controls what material leaves for the vendor and what is expected back.

cards.title: Vendor, service lines and commercial checks on service orders
cards.body:
Vendor, vendor location and subcontract location are mandatory; an inter-unit vendor forces an inter-unit order.
At least one service is required with a positive quantity and continuous sequence numbers.
The first sequence needs an issuable input and the last a primary output, with warehouse and valuation basis defined.
Pay-to, billed-to and payment mode are required, validity cannot precede the order date, and CGST and SGST apply only within a state and IGST only across states.

cards.title: Request balances, multi-level approval and authorisation effects
cards.body:
Quantities drawn from service requests must be positive and within the request balance, request lines of different products cannot be mixed, and the same item must keep the same rate.
A service of repair nature needs an issuable or repairable item, and repairable items cannot be mixed with output items or used on activity and conversion orders.
The order may not exceed the pre-calculated estimate, and on authorisation the finance mapping of items is verified.
Under multi-level approval an approval group is required, only listed users may update a released order, rejections need comments, and Authorized can only follow final-level approval; changing net amount resets the group.
Each save rewrites the version and live order, recalculates request balances and, when authorised, sets output rates; any failure rolls the save back.

items.title: Service Order Amendment
items.context: Material Management › Service and Subcontract Procurement › Service Order Amendment

cards.title: Why a Service Order Amendment is used
cards.body:
A Service Order Amendment changes an authorised service order through a numbered version with its own date, reason and status.
It is used when rate, quantity, schedule, tax or terms change after the order was sent to the vendor.
Order history is kept version by version, and the live order shows the last authorised version.

cards.title: Eligible orders and details required on an amendment
cards.body:
Only orders whose latest version is authorised, that are active and not letters of intent, can be amended, so a pending draft must be completed first.
The amendment date cannot precede the order date and must pass back-dating control, and a reason and status are mandatory.
Request quantities, services, items, shipping, accounts and GST rules are validated as on the original order.
Payment terms and account details reach the live order only when the amendment is authorised.

cards.title: Approval and rejection effects on the live service order
cards.body:
Under multi-level approval an approval group is required, only listed users may update a released amendment, and Authorized cannot be chosen directly.
Final approval copies the amendment onto the live order and reactivates every live line.
Rejection resets the amendment to Initial and also returns the live order to an unauthorised Initial state, so no work proceeds on a disputed version until it is corrected.
An authorised amendment cannot be saved again, and the authorisation step runs on every save.
Concurrency is checked so two people cannot overwrite each other's changes, and freight details are required even when a freight order is linked.

items.title: Bill of Quantity
items.context: Material Management › Service and Subcontract Procurement › Bill of Quantity

cards.title: What a Bill of Quantity fixes for subcontracting
cards.body:
A Bill of Quantity fixes, against a service order or a purchase order item, the exact material to be issued to the subcontractor and the material expected back.
It records quantities, rates, tolerances and the percentage split of output items.
Issues to and receipts from the subcontractor are then controlled against an agreed list.

cards.title: Issue and receipt lists, item flows and output split
cards.body:
The issue list accepts issuable inputs and repairable items, while the receipt list accepts returnable inputs and primary and secondary outputs.
Each line needs an item flow, an item and a quantity, and a returnable input needs a matching issuable input.
Primary and secondary outputs need a split percentage, and outputs of each service or activity must total one hundred percent.
Tolerance needs plus or minus values once a basis is chosen, never above one hundred percent, and the document date cannot precede the order date.

cards.title: Protecting moved quantities and replacing service order lines
cards.body:
Quantities cannot be reduced below what has already been issued or received, and lines with movement cannot be deleted.
For purchase order bills, a line cannot be cut below goods receipt plus gate entry quantity.
Status only moves forward: a released bill cannot return to Initial and an authorised one cannot return to Release.
Only authorised, open service orders at their latest amendment, without a pending unauthorised bill, are offered.
When authorised for a service order, the order's and amendment's lines and request splits are replaced by the bill's lines and the order authorisation is re-run; any failure rolls back everything.
This makes the bill the governing definition of material flow with the subcontractor.

items.title: Service Receipt Note
items.context: Material Management › Service and Subcontract Procurement › Service Receipt Note

cards.title: Purpose of the Service Receipt Note
cards.body:
The Service Receipt Note records services performed and material returned by a subcontractor or service vendor against one or more orders.
It is prepared when work is completed or material comes back against a service order, purchase order, gate entry or inter-unit dispatch challan.
It updates order balances, brings accepted material into stock and proposes an accrual voucher.

cards.title: Reference selection and receipt quantity checks
cards.body:
Vendor and location are mandatory, and at least one reference must be selected; selected references must share source type, expense mapping and subcontract type.
Accepted quantity is received less rejected less free quantity, and amount is accepted quantity times rate.
Challan and received quantities are mandatory, free and replaceable quantities cannot exceed received quantity, and a warehouse is required.
Vendor bill and challan numbers and dates must be given together and cannot be later than the receipt date; receiving over tolerance is warned or blocked.

cards.title: Stock posting by quantity type, inspection and accrual accounting
cards.body:
On authorisation, accepted quantity goes to a normal lot, repairable items to reusable stock, rejected quantity to a rejected lot and replaceable quantity to a replaceable lot linked to the accepted lot; free quantity is received at zero rate.
For conversion work, the lot rate is replaced by the service order item rate where the valuation basis requires it.
Receipts needing inspection cannot be authorised without intimation and inspection, and rejected quantity cannot exceed what inspection recorded.
Where gate-pass control applies, repairable job-work items need a gate pass, and orders with outgoing material need an authorised material issue.
The voucher debits stock or expense against work-in-progress and suspense accounts, with no vendor line, and must match lot values.
Every save recalculates the service order line as completed or partly received.
